2-chronicles-6:14:16.summary: Solomon praises God’s “great mercy” to David, who “walked before Thee” with uprightness of heart.
2-chronicles-6:14:16.why: Same speaker, same mercy and walking language.

2-chronicles-6:14:18.summary: Jacob’s altar to “the God of Israel” shares only the divine title.

2-chronicles-6:14:19.summary: God tells Abram “be pleasing before Me, and be blameless”; the Greek lacks “walk,” leaving only a loose ethical parallel.

2-chronicles-6:14:20.summary: “Who is a God like Thee” who desires mercy and keeps faith with the fathers echoes Solomon’s confession.

2-chronicles-6:14:21.summary: The divine name as “God of your fathers” shares only a general title.

2-chronicles-6:14:22.summary: Daniel addresses God “keeping the covenant and mercy for those who love Thee,” the same formula.

2-chronicles-6:14:23.summary: “There is none like Thee among gods, Lord” matches Solomon’s confession closely.

2-chronicles-6:14:24.summary: David says “there is none like Thee and no God besides Thee,” the same confession his son repeats.

2-chronicles-6:14:25.summary: David blesses the Lord God of Israel before the assembly, a general prayer parallel.

2-chronicles-6:14:26.summary: God showing mercy and remembering His covenant overlaps thematically with covenant-and-mercy language.
2-chronicles-6:14:26.why: Covenant mercy theme in Zechariah’s song.

2-chronicles-6:14:27.summary: Jeremiah’s statement that the Creator is Jacob’s portion shares nothing specific with Solomon’s confession.

2-chronicles-6:14:28.summary: The Lord’s mercy toward those “who keep His covenant” parallels covenant-and-mercy for faithful servants.

2-chronicles-6:14:29.summary: Jacob’s renaming as Israel shares only the name “Israel.”

2-chronicles-6:15:0.summary: God’s promise that David’s son Solomon would build His house is the promise Solomon says was fulfilled.

2-chronicles-6:15:1.summary: God’s promise to raise up David’s seed is the word Solomon says God spoke and fulfilled.

2-chronicles-6:16:0.summary: David recalls the promise that if sons “guard their way” a man shall not be cut off from Israel’s throne, the same condition.

2-chronicles-6:16:1.summary: If David’s sons keep the covenant, their sons will sit on his throne, the same conditional promise.
2-chronicles-6:16:1.why: Psalm version of the dynastic promise.

2-chronicles-6:16:2.summary: Jesus’ words about friends who obey His commands share no specific link to the Davidic throne promise.

2-chronicles-6:16:3.summary: God’s reply repeats that “a man leading in Israel will not be removed from you,” answering this very request.

2-chronicles-6:16:4.summary: Nathan’s oracle promising David’s throne set upright forever is the promise Solomon invokes.

2-chronicles-6:16:5.summary: “Those who walk in the Lord’s law” shares the walking-in-the-law phrase only generally.
2-chronicles-6:16:5.why: General echo of walking in God’s law.

2-chronicles-6:16:6.summary: Ezekiel’s promise to multiply Israel shares no specific link with the dynastic promise.

2-chronicles-6:17:0.summary: God establishing His oath to the fathers, answered by “May it be, Lord,” loosely parallels asking God to confirm His word.
2-chronicles-6:17:0.why: Similar appeal to God’s confirmed promise.

2-chronicles-6:17:1.summary: David prays “confirm for ever the word Thou hast spoken concerning Thy servant,” the same request Solomon repeats.
2-chronicles-6:17:1.why: David’s parallel prayer for the promise.

2-chronicles-6:17:2.summary: Earlier in the same speech Solomon blesses the God of Israel who spoke to David and fulfilled it.
2-chronicles-6:17:2.why: Same promise framed within Solomon’s speech.

2-chronicles-6:17:3.summary: Isaiah’s oracle to Cyrus shares only the title “Israel’s God.”

2-chronicles-6:17:4.summary: The same prayer opens with “Lord, Israel’s God,” a repeated address within the prayer.
2-chronicles-6:17:4.why: Repeated invocation in the same prayer.

2-chronicles-6:17:5.summary: God’s promise to answer the thirsty poor shares only the title “God of Israel.”

2-chronicles-6:17:6.summary: The vision of the God of Israel at Sinai shares only the divine title.

2-chronicles-6:18:0.summary: “Heaven and the heaven of heaven cannot bear His glory” repeats Solomon’s own question about building God a house.
2-chronicles-6:18:0.why: Solomon’s earlier statement of the same idea.

2-chronicles-6:18:1.summary: “What sort of house will you build for Me?” since heaven is His throne, parallels Solomon’s question.
2-chronicles-6:18:1.why: Prophetic restatement of God’s transcendence over the temple.

2-chronicles-6:18:2.summary: God present in heaven and Hades expresses His omnipresence, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:18:3.summary: Paul’s “third heaven” shares only the word heaven with Solomon’s question.

2-chronicles-6:18:4.summary: Sennacherib’s taunt about gods unable to save has no link to God’s dwelling.

2-chronicles-6:18:5.summary: God dwelling on high yet looking upon lowly things loosely parallels the transcendent God attending to earth.

2-chronicles-6:18:6.summary: Stephen quotes “Heaven is My throne… What kind of house will you build for Me” to show God does not dwell in handmade things.
2-chronicles-6:18:6.why: New Testament use of the same theme.

2-chronicles-6:18:7.summary: God, Lord of heaven and earth, “does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands,” echoing Solomon’s question.
2-chronicles-6:18:7.why: Paul’s statement of the same truth.

2-chronicles-6:18:8.summary: Human lowliness before God’s purity loosely relates to the wonder that God would dwell with mortals.

2-chronicles-6:18:9.summary: The Father giving good gifts shares no specific link with God’s dwelling.

2-chronicles-6:18:10.summary: God ascending and receiving gifts “to establish a dwelling” loosely touches God’s dwelling among people.

2-chronicles-6:18:11.summary: Humans in “houses of clay” is a different image about human frailty, not God’s dwelling.

2-chronicles-6:18:12.summary: In the Greek God will be “called upon among the sons of Israel,” lacking the dwelling wording but near the presence theme.

2-chronicles-6:18:14.summary: The Most High dwelling in the heights yet giving life to the lowly loosely parallels God’s transcendence and nearness.
2-chronicles-6:18:14.why: Transcendence with care for the humble.

2-chronicles-6:18:15.summary: Job’s fear that God would sift his words shares nothing with the source.

2-chronicles-6:18:16.summary: God filling “the heaven and the earth” parallels the idea that heaven cannot contain Him only thematically.

2-chronicles-6:19:8.summary: Daniel asks God to “hear Thy servant’s prayer and my supplications,” closely matching Solomon’s wording.
2-chronicles-6:19:8.why: Later prayer with the same appeal.

2-chronicles-6:19:1.summary: “Lord, hear my voice” asks God to attend to petition, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:19:2.summary: A prayer that the Lord hear and help from the sanctuary relates generally to temple prayer.

2-chronicles-6:19:3.summary: “Look upon Thy covenant” shares only the request for God to look.

2-chronicles-6:19:4.summary: The parable of the persistent widow shares only a general theme of prayer.

2-chronicles-6:19:5.summary: “Hear my prayer” is a general petition parallel.

2-chronicles-6:19:6.summary: “Attend to the voice of my petition… unto Thee I will pray” loosely parallels Solomon’s plea.

2-chronicles-6:19:7.summary: Jesus’ prayer for future believers has no specific link to Solomon’s plea.

2-chronicles-6:20:0.summary: The Lord’s eyes and ears toward the righteous’ supplication parallels the open eyes requested, generally.

2-chronicles-6:20:1.summary: God as guard and shelter shares nothing specific with eyes open toward the house.

2-chronicles-6:20:2.summary: God chose Jerusalem “for My name to be there,” the place where Solomon says the name would be invoked.
2-chronicles-6:20:2.why: The choice of the place for God’s name.

2-chronicles-6:20:3.summary: Daniel prays toward Jerusalem from exile, practicing prayer directed toward the chosen place.
2-chronicles-6:20:3.why: Shows prayer toward this place in practice.

2-chronicles-6:20:4.summary: “The place which the Lord… shall choose for His name to be called upon” is the Deuteronomic basis of the source.
2-chronicles-6:20:4.why: Background for the place of the name.

2-chronicles-6:20:5.summary: Nehemiah asks God’s “eyes opened to hear Thy servant’s prayer… day and night,” echoing Solomon’s wording.
2-chronicles-6:20:5.why: Later prayer reusing the same request.

2-chronicles-6:20:6.summary: “The place… for His name to be called upon there” matches the place where God’s name is invoked.

2-chronicles-6:20:8.summary: The Lord’s eyes looking throughout the earth share the eyes image only generally.
2-chronicles-6:20:8.why: General image of God’s watching eyes.

2-chronicles-6:20:9.summary: Hezekiah prays “Open Thine eyes, Lord… hear,” echoing the open eyes and hearing Solomon asks for.
2-chronicles-6:20:9.why: Later royal prayer with the same appeal.

2-chronicles-6:20:10.summary: The fullness of deity dwelling in Christ has no specific link to the temple prayer.

2-chronicles-6:21:0.summary: God passing over impieties because He desires mercy relates to forgiveness only generally.

2-chronicles-6:21:1.summary: God wiping out lawless acts relates generally to the plea to be propitious.

2-chronicles-6:21:2.summary: “Lord, be propitious! Lord, hear” closely echoes “hear and be propitious.”
2-chronicles-6:21:2.why: Later prayer with the same plea.

2-chronicles-6:21:3.summary: The same prayer repeats “hear from heaven, from Thy… dwelling place… be propitious.”

2-chronicles-6:21:4.summary: “With Thee is atonement” relates to forgiveness thematically.

2-chronicles-6:21:5.summary: The priests’ prayer “came to His holy dwelling place, to heaven,” showing the answer Solomon asks for.
2-chronicles-6:21:5.why: Fulfillment of prayer heard from heaven.

2-chronicles-6:21:6.summary: The Most High dwelling in the heights loosely parallels God’s heavenly dwelling.

2-chronicles-6:21:7.summary: “Forgive us our debts” shares the plea for forgiveness only generally.

2-chronicles-6:21:8.summary: “God is in heaven and you are on earth” loosely parallels hearing from heaven.

2-chronicles-6:21:9.summary: Addressing the Father “in the heavens” loosely parallels prayer to God in heaven.

2-chronicles-6:21:10.summary: “Thou who dwellest in heaven” shares the heavenly-dwelling image generally.

2-chronicles-6:21:11.summary: God dwelling on high and observing shares only a loose image.

2-chronicles-6:21:12.summary: God wiping away sins like a cloud relates to forgiveness generally.

2-chronicles-6:21:13.summary: “Thou forgavest Thy people” relates generally to the plea for forgiveness of Israel.
2-chronicles-6:21:13.why: Example of God forgiving His people.

2-chronicles-6:22:0.summary: An oath by God between neighbors over a dispute matches the neighbor’s oath before the altar.
2-chronicles-6:22:0.why: Legal background for the oath case.

2-chronicles-6:22:1.summary: Jesus discusses swearing “by the altar,” sharing the altar-oath idea but not the judicial setting.

2-chronicles-6:22:2.summary: A solemn adjuration binding a witness relates generally to oath-curses.

2-chronicles-6:22:3.summary: The priest’s oath-curse at the sanctuary relates generally to oath-curses taken before God.

2-chronicles-6:22:4.summary: Swearing by God’s name falsely shares only the oath theme.

2-chronicles-6:23:0.summary: The righteous person’s righteousness upon him and the lawless person’s lawlessness upon him matches Solomon’s request.

2-chronicles-6:23:1.summary: Woe to the lawless, evils according to their works, loosely parallels repaying the lawless.

2-chronicles-6:23:2.summary: God repaying Babylon shares only the repayment theme.

2-chronicles-6:23:3.summary: Distress for evildoers and glory for the good parallels just recompense generally.

2-chronicles-6:23:4.summary: Condemns judging the righteous unjust, the opposite of justifying the righteous.

2-chronicles-6:23:5.summary: Judges “justify the righteous, and condemn the ungodly,” the same judicial language.
2-chronicles-6:23:5.why: Legal standard Solomon applies to God.

2-chronicles-6:23:6.summary: God repaying Ahab for Naboth’s blood shares the repayment theme.

2-chronicles-6:23:7.summary: Hananiah’s death sentence shares no specific link to the source.

2-chronicles-6:23:8.summary: Eating the fruit of their own way loosely matches “returning his ways upon his own head.”

2-chronicles-6:23:9.summary: The curse taking effect on the guilty woman relates generally to oath-curses judged by God.

2-chronicles-6:23:10.summary: God seeing trouble and helping the orphan has no specific link to judging oaths.

2-chronicles-6:24:0.summary: God’s curse “you shall fall before your enemies” is the defeat Solomon envisions after sin.

2-chronicles-6:24:1.summary: Seeking God in distress and returning to Him who will not forsake matches return after defeat.

2-chronicles-6:24:2.summary: Being given “to slaughter before your enemies” is the covenant curse the source anticipates.

2-chronicles-6:24:3.summary: Israel shall “confess their sins” and God will remember the covenant, matching confession after defeat.

2-chronicles-6:24:4.summary: Daniel’s confession prayer after defeat and exile enacts Solomon’s scenario (truncated range judged on shown text).
2-chronicles-6:24:4.why: Later example of confession after defeat.

2-chronicles-6:24:5.summary: Israel’s sins leading to judgment relate generally, but the shown text has no return or confession.
2-chronicles-6:24:5.why: Background of sin leading to defeat.

2-chronicles-6:24:6.summary: Israel “turned its back before its enemy” describes defeat, without the sin-and-return elements.

2-chronicles-6:24:7.summary: The shown text of Isaiah 63 concerns God’s vengeance on Edom; the truncated prayer is not visible.
2-chronicles-6:24:7.why: Shown text does not carry the link.

2-chronicles-6:24:8.summary: Ezra confesses that for their sins they were handed over to kings of the nations, praying at the temple.

2-chronicles-6:24:9.summary: God calls Israel to return and recognize its injustice, a general return-and-confess parallel.

2-chronicles-6:24:10.summary: If Israel turns back, God will gather them to “the place I chose for My name,” matching return and prayer.
2-chronicles-6:24:10.why: Promise tied to the chosen place.

2-chronicles-6:24:11.summary: Israel “confessed their sins” and worshiped, enacting return and confession (truncated range).

2-chronicles-6:24:12.summary: “Thou didst turn us backward before our enemies” describes defeat, without sin or return.

2-chronicles-6:24:13.summary: When Israel returns to the Lord after curses, He will have mercy and gather them.

2-chronicles-6:24:14.summary: Israel doing evil before the Lord describes sin generally.

2-chronicles-6:24:15.summary: Because of sin Israel “could not stand before their enemies,” generally parallel.

2-chronicles-6:24:16.summary: Not being able to withstand enemies is a general covenant-curse parallel.

2-chronicles-6:24:17.summary: Israel cannot stand before its enemies because the people sinned, a specific case of sin causing defeat.
2-chronicles-6:24:17.why: Classic example of defeat due to sin.

2-chronicles-6:24:18.summary: Serving enemies as a covenant curse relates generally to defeat.

2-chronicles-6:24:20.summary: The one who explains reproofs being loved loosely parallels confession.

2-chronicles-6:25:0.summary: God promises to bring back exiles, cleanse sins, and not remember them, matching forgiveness and return to the land.
2-chronicles-6:25:0.why: Prophetic promise of the same restoration.

2-chronicles-6:25:1.summary: Cyrus’ decree allowing return to Jerusalem is a historical return, but no forgiveness language is shown.

2-chronicles-6:25:2.summary: The Lord gave Israel “all the land that He had sworn to give their fathers,” the land Solomon mentions.
2-chronicles-6:25:2.why: The land given to the fathers.

2-chronicles-6:25:3.summary: God, after handing His people to nations, remembered His covenant and granted compassion, matching forgiveness after defeat (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:25:4.summary: The land promised to Abraham’s seed relates to the land given to the fathers.

2-chronicles-6:25:5.summary: God bringing Israel into the land sworn to the fathers relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:26:0.summary: God making “your heaven iron” for disobedience is the drought curse behind the closed heaven.

2-chronicles-6:26:1.summary: “The heaven above your head shall be bronze” describes the same withholding of rain for sin.

2-chronicles-6:26:2.summary: God will “shut up heaven, so that there is no rain” in anger at sin, the same wording.

2-chronicles-6:26:3.summary: Elijah announces neither dew nor rain, a drought sent against Ahab’s Israel.

2-chronicles-6:26:4.summary: Priests weep at the altar and pray “Spare Thy people” in calamity, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:26:5.summary: God sending famine on a land that sins relates generally to drought for sin.

2-chronicles-6:26:6.summary: Manasseh humbled himself when afflicted, prayed, and was heard, a general pattern parallel.
2-chronicles-6:26:6.why: Example of affliction leading to prayer.

2-chronicles-6:26:7.summary: The witnesses “shut heaven, so that rain may not fall,” sharing the distinctive image.

2-chronicles-6:26:8.summary: God withheld rain, “yet you did not turn to Me,” the very purpose of drought in the source (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:26:9.summary: Turning from impieties to live parallels turning from sins generally.

2-chronicles-6:26:10.summary: God commanding clouds not to rain on His vineyard parallels drought as judgment.
2-chronicles-6:26:10.why: Image of rain withheld in judgment.

2-chronicles-6:26:11.summary: In affliction they will seek God’s face and return, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:26:12.summary: Sold for sins and God drying up waters relates loosely to drought for sin.

2-chronicles-6:26:13.summary: Confessing rather than covering sin parallels turning from sin generally.

2-chronicles-6:26:14.summary: Jeremiah’s lament over “the lack of rain” with confession of sin parallels the drought scenario (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:26:15.summary: Priests gather the people into God’s house to cry to the Lord as crops fail (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:26:16.summary: Jesus recalls when “heaven was shut” in Elijah’s day, the same image of drought.
2-chronicles-6:26:16.why: New Testament reference to shut heaven.

2-chronicles-6:27:0.summary: God “gives us early and late rain,” a general parallel to the plea for rain.

2-chronicles-6:27:1.summary: “Ask the Lord for rain in its season” parallels Solomon’s plea that God give rain.

2-chronicles-6:27:3.summary: God teaching from His law loosely parallels making known the good way.

2-chronicles-6:27:4.summary: God giving instruction in the way loosely parallels teaching the good way.

2-chronicles-6:27:5.summary: After Baal’s prophets are destroyed, Elijah prays and rain returns, an example of rain restored (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:27:6.summary: “They shall all be taught by God” relates loosely to God teaching His people.

2-chronicles-6:27:7.summary: “Tell us the way we should go” echoes the phrasing of the way to walk loosely.

2-chronicles-6:27:8.summary: God sets apart rain “for Thine inheritance,” pairing rain and inheritance as in the source.

2-chronicles-6:27:9.summary: God directing clouds for discipline or mercy relates loosely to rain and judgment.

2-chronicles-6:27:10.summary: God showing His way so that people walk in His paths parallels teaching the way.

2-chronicles-6:27:11.summary: Elijah prayed and “heaven gave rain,” illustrating prayer answered with rain.
2-chronicles-6:27:11.why: NT example of prayer for rain.

2-chronicles-6:27:12.summary: “See which is the good way, and walk in it” closely parallels “the good way in which they should walk.”
2-chronicles-6:27:12.why: Same phrase about the good way.

2-chronicles-6:27:13.summary: Heaven answering the earth with grain loosely relates to restored rain.

2-chronicles-6:27:14.summary: God giving “rain of blessing” parallels the plea for rain generally.

2-chronicles-6:27:15.summary: Only God brings rain, said in a drought prayer, relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:27:16.summary: In the Greek wording “This is the way” is spoken by those who led astray, reversing the link the label assumes.
2-chronicles-6:27:16.why: Greek wording does not carry the link.

2-chronicles-6:27:17.summary: God will rain early and late rainfall, a general rain-restoration parallel.

2-chronicles-6:27:18.summary: “Make Thy ways known to me, Lord, and teach me Thy paths” echoes God making known the way.

2-chronicles-6:27:19.summary: “He will give sinners instruction in the way” matches God teaching sinners the good way.

2-chronicles-6:27:20.summary: “Instruct me, Lord, in the way” is a general instruction parallel.

2-chronicles-6:28:0.summary: A famine in the land is a general instance of the calamity named.

2-chronicles-6:28:1.summary: Apocalyptic locusts from the abyss share only the word locust.

2-chronicles-6:28:2.summary: Locusts, bruchus locust, blight, and caterpillar repeat the plague list in Solomon’s prayer.

2-chronicles-6:28:3.summary: “Is anyone suffering? Let him pray” relates generally to prayer in suffering.
2-chronicles-6:28:3.why: General call to pray in trouble.
2-chronicles-6:28:3.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

2-chronicles-6:28:4.summary: Covenant curses list death, “wind blight,” “pallor,” and defeat by enemies, matching Solomon’s calamities (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:28:5.summary: Joel’s caterpillar, locust, bruchus locust, and blight match the source’s plague list.

2-chronicles-6:28:6.summary: Hezekiah’s prayer in illness relates generally to prayer in suffering.

2-chronicles-6:28:7.summary: A siege causing famine in Samaria illustrates both calamities, without prayer elements.

2-chronicles-6:28:8.summary: The locust plague on Egypt relates only through locusts.

2-chronicles-6:28:9.summary: Jehoshaphat recalls the promise that in calamity—sword, death, famine—they would stand before this house and be heard.

2-chronicles-6:28:10.summary: Sennacherib camping against Judah’s cities illustrates the enemy before their cities.

2-chronicles-6:28:11.summary: Sousakim seizes fortified cities because they had sinned, a general example.

2-chronicles-6:28:12.summary: Covenant curses of death, enemies, cities, and scarcity of bread match the source’s calamities.

2-chronicles-6:28:13.summary: Jaundice and enemies eating crops loosely parallel yellowing and oppression.

2-chronicles-6:28:14.summary: Failed wheat and barley harvest relates generally to crop disaster.

2-chronicles-6:28:15.summary: A seven-year famine called upon the land is a general example.

2-chronicles-6:29:0.summary: The heart perceiving its sorrow loosely echoes a man knowing his own affliction.

2-chronicles-6:29:1.summary: Declaring one’s affliction before the Lord parallels individual prayer in trouble.

2-chronicles-6:29:2.summary: The Lord looking down from heaven on all people relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:29:3.summary: God hears the one who calls in affliction, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:29:4.summary: “Call on Me in the day of affliction” parallels prayer in trouble generally.

2-chronicles-6:29:5.summary: Solomon himself “spread out his hands,” the gesture he now describes for any petitioner.
2-chronicles-6:29:5.why: Same gesture within the same scene.

2-chronicles-6:29:6.summary: Confessing sin and every holy one praying parallels personal confession generally.

2-chronicles-6:29:7.summary: “Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me” God will not listen, contrasting with heard outstretched hands.
2-chronicles-6:29:7.why: Shows when outstretched prayer is refused.

2-chronicles-6:30:0.summary: “The Lord examines every heart and knows every thought,” spoken to Solomon, parallels God alone knowing hearts.
2-chronicles-6:30:0.why: David taught Solomon the same truth.

2-chronicles-6:30:1.summary: “God looks at the heart” parallels God knowing the heart of men.

2-chronicles-6:30:2.summary: Christ “searcheth kidneys and hearts” and gives “each… according to your works,” matching both clauses.

2-chronicles-6:30:3.summary: The Son of Man will “repay each person according to his conduct,” matching giving each according to his ways.

2-chronicles-6:30:4.summary: All things laid open to God’s eyes relates generally to God knowing hearts.

2-chronicles-6:30:5.summary: “Thou wilt repay each one according to his works” closely parallels the recompense clause.

2-chronicles-6:30:6.summary: The Lord in heaven whose eyelids “examine the sons of men” parallels God in heaven knowing hearts.

2-chronicles-6:30:7.summary: God examines hearts “to give each according to his ways,” matching both clauses closely.
2-chronicles-6:30:7.why: Same pairing of heart-knowledge and recompense.

2-chronicles-6:30:9.summary: Jesus “knew what was within a person,” paralleling knowledge of the human heart.

2-chronicles-6:30:10.summary: “I will judge you, each according to his way” matches giving to each according to his ways.

2-chronicles-6:30:11.summary: “Thou examinest hearts,” in David’s prayer, matches God knowing hearts.

2-chronicles-6:30:12.summary: God repaying the psalmist according to his righteousness relates to recompense generally.

2-chronicles-6:31:0.summary: “Only fear the Lord” shares the fear theme generally.

2-chronicles-6:31:1.summary: “Who fear the Lord, who walk in His ways” pairs fear and God’s ways as in the source.

2-chronicles-6:31:2.summary: Reverence for God as wisdom relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:31:3.summary: The Church walking in the fear of the Lord relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:31:4.summary: God testing so that His fear may be in them relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:31:5.summary: The Greek “with Thee is atonement” lacks the fear clause the English label relies on.
2-chronicles-6:31:5.why: Greek wording does not carry the link.

2-chronicles-6:32:0.summary: Foreigners attached to the Lord are brought to God’s house of prayer (truncated), matching the foreigner who prays.
2-chronicles-6:32:0.why: Prophetic welcome of foreigners at the temple.

2-chronicles-6:32:2.summary: Many coming from east and west to the kingdom loosely parallels foreigners coming from afar.

2-chronicles-6:32:3.summary: Greeks “going up to worship at the feast” illustrates foreigners coming to worship.

2-chronicles-6:32:4.summary: Nations go up to Jerusalem yearly to bow before the Lord, matching foreigners coming to pray.

2-chronicles-6:32:5.summary: Strangers far away brought near in Christ loosely parallels the foreigner from a distant land.

2-chronicles-6:32:6.summary: The God-fearing foreigner Cornelius prays and his prayers rise before God.
2-chronicles-6:32:6.why: Example of a foreigner’s heard prayer.

2-chronicles-6:32:7.summary: Many nations will come to seek the Lord in Jerusalem, matching foreigners coming to pray.

2-chronicles-6:32:8.summary: An Ethiopian official “had come to Jerusalem to worship,” a foreigner from a distant land.
2-chronicles-6:32:8.why: NT example of a distant foreigner worshiping.

2-chronicles-6:32:9.summary: God’s “strong hand” and stretched-out hand loosely echo the mighty hand and uplifted arm.

2-chronicles-6:32:10.summary: Laws for the resident foreigner at Passover relate generally to foreigners in worship.

2-chronicles-6:32:11.summary: Foreign visitors at Pentecost loosely parallel foreigners coming to Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-6:32:12.summary: Nations and children come from far away to Jerusalem’s light (truncated), matching foreigners drawn from afar.

2-chronicles-6:32:13.summary: The Gibeonites came “from a very distant land” because they “heard His name,” closely echoing the source.
2-chronicles-6:32:13.why: Same wording of distant land and God’s name.

2-chronicles-6:32:14.summary: Brothers brought from all nations to Jerusalem relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:32:15.summary: Magi from the east arriving in Jerusalem loosely parallels foreigners coming.

2-chronicles-6:32:16.summary: Other sheep not of this fold loosely parallels foreigners included.

2-chronicles-6:32:17.summary: “With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out” shares the mighty-hand phrase only.

2-chronicles-6:32:18.summary: Ruth the foreigner adopting Israel’s God is a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:32:19.summary: The queen of Sheba heard “the Lord’s name” and came to Jerusalem, a foreigner drawn by God’s name.
2-chronicles-6:32:19.why: Example of a foreigner drawn by the name.

2-chronicles-6:32:20.summary: God’s arm and raised right hand loosely echo the uplifted arm.

2-chronicles-6:32:21.summary: A captive girl pointing her foreign master to Israel’s prophet relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:32:22.summary: The queen of the south came from the ends of the earth, but to hear Solomon’s wisdom, not to pray.

2-chronicles-6:32:23.summary: Naaman confesses “there is no God in all the earth except in Israel,” a foreigner coming to know God.

2-chronicles-6:32:24.summary: Jethro hears of God’s deeds and confesses Him, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-6:32:25.summary: Rahab knows the Lord gave the land, a foreigner aware of God’s power.

2-chronicles-6:32:26.summary: Ruth came to a people she had not known, trusting under God’s wings.

2-chronicles-6:32:27.summary: Naaman to learn there is a prophet in Israel relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:33:0.summary: God promises to “hear from heaven” for the people “upon whom My name has been invoked,” answering the prayer.

2-chronicles-6:33:2.summary: The barren woman enlarging her tent shares no specific link.

2-chronicles-6:33:3.summary: “That Thy way may be known on earth… among all nations” matches all peoples knowing God’s name.
2-chronicles-6:33:3.why: Same aim of universal knowledge of God.

2-chronicles-6:33:4.summary: Putting God’s name upon Israel loosely relates to the name invoked.
2-chronicles-6:33:4.why: God’s name placed on His people.

2-chronicles-6:33:5.summary: All the earth’s ends turning to the Lord relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:33:6.summary: The servant as a light for nations relates loosely to all peoples knowing God.

2-chronicles-6:33:7.summary: All earth’s kings thanking the Lord relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:33:8.summary: “All the kingdoms of the earth will know that Thou art the Lord” matches the aim that all peoples know God.

2-chronicles-6:33:9.summary: Nations hoping in Jesse’s root relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:33:10.summary: The world’s kingdom becoming Christ’s shares no specific link.

2-chronicles-6:33:11.summary: God chose Jerusalem to build “a house for My name,” matching the house over which God’s name is invoked.
2-chronicles-6:33:11.why: Parallel speech on the house for the name.

2-chronicles-6:33:12.summary: “All the earth will know that there is a God in Israel” matches the aim that all peoples know God.

2-chronicles-6:33:13.summary: God exalted among the nations relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:34:0.summary: Facing invasion, Jehoshaphat prays at the house built for God’s name, recalling this promise.
2-chronicles-6:34:0.why: Example of war prayer at the temple.

2-chronicles-6:34:1.summary: God’s promise to Joshua of victory relates generally to war under God.

2-chronicles-6:34:2.summary: Asa, going out against an enemy, cries to the Lord and is given victory.
2-chronicles-6:34:2.why: Example of prayer in battle answered.

2-chronicles-6:34:3.summary: Solomon’s Greek-only words about the house shares only the house theme.

2-chronicles-6:34:4.summary: Daniel prays toward Jerusalem, matching prayer toward the chosen city.
2-chronicles-6:34:4.why: Example of prayer toward the city.

2-chronicles-6:34:5.summary: God “chose Jerusalem for My name,” the chosen city referenced in the source.

2-chronicles-6:34:6.summary: Hezekiah and Isaiah pray during invasion and God destroys the Assyrian army.

2-chronicles-6:34:7.summary: Israel sent to battle Midian by God relates loosely to war on God’s errand.

2-chronicles-6:34:8.summary: God sending Saul against Amalek relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:34:9.summary: Israel inquiring of the Lord before battle relates loosely.

2-chronicles-6:34:10.summary: The Lord founded Zion as refuge relates loosely to the chosen city.

2-chronicles-6:34:11.summary: “The Lord sent you on a mission” against Amalek echoes the way God sends them.

2-chronicles-6:34:12.summary: “When you go forth unto war against your enemies” God goes with you, matching the source.

2-chronicles-6:34:13.summary: God sending Joshua against Ai relates loosely (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:34:15.summary: Jehoshaphat cried out in battle and the Lord saved him, a general example.

2-chronicles-6:34:16.summary: Judah assembling to seek the Lord relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:35:0.summary: “Thou hast upheld my judgment and my cause” matches “uphold their right” against enemies.
2-chronicles-6:35:0.why: Psalm of God upholding the cause.

2-chronicles-6:35:1.summary: Leaders failing to judge the orphan’s case contrasts with God upholding right.

2-chronicles-6:35:2.summary: God tells Hezekiah, “I heard what you prayed,” answering prayer against an invader (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:35:3.summary: Daniel asks God to hear “prayer and my supplications,” echoing the source’s wording.
2-chronicles-6:35:3.why: Same plea for prayer and supplication.

2-chronicles-6:36:0.summary: “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves” matches “no human being who will not sin.”

2-chronicles-6:36:1.summary: “No righteous person on earth who will… not sin” closely matches the source’s parenthesis.

2-chronicles-6:36:2.summary: “We all stumble in many things” parallels universal sinfulness.

2-chronicles-6:36:3.summary: “What mortal can be blameless” parallels universal sinfulness.

2-chronicles-6:36:4.summary: If God marks lawless deeds, “who will withstand?” parallels universal sin.

2-chronicles-6:36:5.summary: “No one living will be justified before Thee” parallels universal sin.

2-chronicles-6:36:6.summary: Israel forsakes the covenant and the Lord removes them from their land (truncated).

2-chronicles-6:36:7.summary: “Who will boast that he has a pure heart?” parallels universal sinfulness.

2-chronicles-6:36:8.summary: Kings’ version of the same prayer asks compassion from “those who took them captive.”

2-chronicles-6:36:9.summary: Israel “was deported from its land to the Assyrians,” fulfilling the captivity foreseen.

2-chronicles-6:36:10.summary: Being led captive into all the nations relates generally.

2-chronicles-6:36:11.summary: The Lord will lead Israel to an unknown nation, the covenant curse of captivity.

2-chronicles-6:36:12.summary: Shame belongs to Israel “near and far” in countries where God scattered them for sin, echoing the source.

2-chronicles-6:36:13.summary: Israel will be in “your enemies’ land” for disobedience (truncated), matching captivity in an enemy land.

2-chronicles-6:36:14.summary: The Lord will scatter Israel among the nations for sin, matching captivity.

2-chronicles-6:36:15.summary: A regnal formula for Manaem has no link to sin or captivity.

2-chronicles-6:36:16.summary: The Assyrian king deported Israel from Samaria, a fulfillment of captivity to a far land.

2-chronicles-6:36:18.summary: The Lord will scatter Israel from one end of the earth to the other, the curse of exile.

2-chronicles-6:36:19.summary: The Lord removed Israel from His presence in anger, the realized exile.

2-chronicles-6:37:5.summary: Both are communal confessions: “we sinned” and “acted lawlessly” appear in each, matching the exiles’ prescribed confession.
2-chronicles-6:37:5.why: Shows the confession formula actually used in Israel’s prayers.

2-chronicles-6:37:0.summary: Ephraim repents “after my captivity” and asks “Turn me back, and I will return,” enacting the turning in captivity Solomon envisions.
2-chronicles-6:37:0.why: Illustrates the repentance in exile Solomon anticipated.

2-chronicles-6:37:1.summary: Isaiah’s confession of “lawless deeds” and being handed over for sins is a general penitential parallel; shown text lacks captivity or turning language.
2-chronicles-6:37:1.why: Another example of national confession of sin.

2-chronicles-6:37:2.summary: Daniel in exile confesses “we have sinned, done wrong, acted impiously,” closely echoing the threefold confession Solomon prescribes.
2-chronicles-6:37:2.why: Daniel fulfills Solomon’s pattern of confession in captivity.

2-chronicles-6:37:3.summary: The prodigal “came to himself” in a far land and resolves to confess “I have sinned”; a loose parable parallel to turning in exile.
2-chronicles-6:37:3.why: Personal parable of repentance from far away.

2-chronicles-6:37:4.summary: Nehemiah’s recital of Israel’s sin, oppression, and crying out to God whom He heard from heaven parallels the cycle Solomon anticipates, but without exile confession wording.
2-chronicles-6:37:4.why: Shows God’s repeated hearing when Israel cried out.

2-chronicles-6:37:6.summary: God calls exiled Israel to “Return” and “recognize your injustice,” promising to bring them into Zion, matching confession and return from captivity.
2-chronicles-6:37:6.why: God’s side of the invitation to repentant exiles.

2-chronicles-6:37:7.summary: Moses foretells that in distress among the nations Israel will seek God with all their heart and “return unto the Lord.”

2-chronicles-6:37:8.summary: Among the nations where scattered, Israel “receive[s] them into your heart” and returns, and God gathers them, closely matching turning heart in exile.
2-chronicles-6:37:8.why: Covenant promise that grounds the prayer.
2-chronicles-6:37:8.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

2-chronicles-6:37:9.summary: A person blames himself for sins and asks deliverance; a general confession parallel without exile or national context.

2-chronicles-6:37:10.summary: Nehemiah, in exile, confesses “we have sinned against Thee” for Israel, enacting the confession Solomon prescribes.
2-chronicles-6:37:10.why: A historical prayer that follows Solomon’s pattern.

2-chronicles-6:37:11.summary: Ezra confesses “lawless deeds” that brought Israel to “captivity” at the kings’ hands, closely matching confession of sin linked to exile.

2-chronicles-6:37:12.summary: In their enemies’ land Israel “shall confess their sins” and God remembers His covenant, the Torah basis for repentance in exile.
2-chronicles-6:37:12.why: Covenant promise behind confession in exile.

2-chronicles-6:38:0.summary: Joel’s call to “turn to Me with your whole heart” parallels returning “with all their heart.”

2-chronicles-6:38:1.summary: Daniel in Babylon sets his face toward God, prays and confesses, exemplifying the exile prayer Solomon describes.
2-chronicles-6:38:1.why: Concrete example of exile prayer and confession.

2-chronicles-6:38:3.summary: Daniel prays with windows open “toward Jerusalem” in exile, literally praying toward the city as Solomon’s petition specifies.
2-chronicles-6:38:3.why: Shows the practice of praying toward Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-6:38:4.summary: Same prayer: praying “toward this city Thou hast chosen and the house I have built for Thy name” appears in both.
2-chronicles-6:38:4.why: Repeated formula within Solomon’s dedication prayer.

2-chronicles-6:38:5.summary: To the exiles God promises that if they pray and seek Him “with your whole heart” He will listen.
2-chronicles-6:38:5.why: God’s promise answering the exiles’ wholehearted prayer.

2-chronicles-6:38:6.summary: Manasseh, taken captive to Babylon, humbles himself and prays, and God hears and restores him, an instance of the scenario Solomon envisioned.
2-chronicles-6:38:6.why: Historical case of a captive’s prayer being heard.

2-chronicles-6:38:7.summary: Hosea calls Israel to “Return… to the Lord your God” with words of confession; a general repentance parallel without exile or prayer-toward language.

2-chronicles-6:39:0.summary: A plea to “forgive all my sins” loosely matches asking God to be propitious toward sinners.

2-chronicles-6:39:1.summary: Micah praises God who removes injustices and pardons sins; thematic match with propitiation, no prayer-hearing language.

2-chronicles-6:39:2.summary: Same refrain: “then hear from heaven their supplication and prayer and uphold their right.”
2-chronicles-6:39:2.why: Repeated petition formula in the same prayer.

2-chronicles-6:39:3.summary: God returns to Jerusalem “in compassion” and rebuilds His house; a loose link to mercy after exile.

2-chronicles-6:40:10.summary: “The Lord’s eyes” and “His ears toward their supplication” echo eyes open and ears attentive to supplication.

2-chronicles-6:40:0.summary: God answers almost verbatim: “My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer of this place.”
2-chronicles-6:40:0.why: God’s direct reply to Solomon’s request.

2-chronicles-6:40:1.summary: God “inclined His ear” to the psalmist; a general image of God hearing prayer.

2-chronicles-6:40:2.summary: A plea to “attend to my petition; give ear to my prayer” shares the request for an attentive ear.
2-chronicles-6:40:2.why: Similar personal plea to be heard.

2-chronicles-6:40:3.summary: Nehemiah asks “let Thine ear be attentive and Thine eyes opened,” closely echoing Solomon’s words.

2-chronicles-6:40:4.summary: Nehemiah repeats “let Thine ear be attentive to Thy servant’s prayer.”

2-chronicles-6:40:5.summary: An oath of innocence about injustice in one’s hands has no link to eyes and ears attentive to prayer.

2-chronicles-6:40:6.summary: A cry to God “attend to me” complaining He does not hear; only a general appeal for God’s attention.

2-chronicles-6:40:7.summary: Daniel prays “Attend with Thine ear… Open Thine eyes,” echoing Solomon’s eyes-open, ears-attentive request.

2-chronicles-6:40:8.summary: Hezekiah asks “Hear, Lord; look, Lord,” appealing to God’s ears and eyes in the temple.
2-chronicles-6:40:8.why: Another king’s plea using eyes and ears.

2-chronicles-6:40:9.summary: “Look; hear me, Lord” is a general plea for God to see and hear.
2-chronicles-6:40:9.why: Similar appeal to God’s sight and hearing.

2-chronicles-6:40:11.summary: “Incline Thine ear to me” shares the plea for an attentive ear, otherwise a personal rescue prayer.

2-chronicles-6:40:12.summary: The psalmist cries day and night before God; only a general theme of persistent prayer.

2-chronicles-6:40:13.summary: “The Lord’s eyes look throughout all the earth” shares the image of God’s eyes, but in a rebuke context.

2-chronicles-6:41:0.summary: “He clothed me in a garment of salvation” and rejoicing echo priests clothed with salvation and sons rejoicing.
2-chronicles-6:41:0.why: Same image of being clothed in salvation.

2-chronicles-6:41:1.summary: David planned “a house of rest for the ark,” matching God’s arising to His rest with the ark.
2-chronicles-6:41:1.why: Background to the ark’s resting place.

2-chronicles-6:41:2.summary: The bride clothed in pure fine linen of righteous acts loosely echoes priests clothed in salvation.

2-chronicles-6:41:3.summary: The rod of power from Zion does not match “ark of Thy strength”; only an incidental power idea.

2-chronicles-6:41:4.summary: The gospel as God’s power for salvation shares only general words, not the clothing or ark imagery.

2-chronicles-6:41:5.summary: A general call to rejoice in the Lord loosely matches sons rejoicing.

2-chronicles-6:41:6.summary: Mourners receive a “robe of glory” and joy; loose parallel to being clothed and rejoicing.

2-chronicles-6:41:7.summary: Putting on the new human in righteousness loosely parallels being clothed with salvation.

2-chronicles-6:41:8.summary: “Put on the Lord Jesus Christ” shares only the clothing metaphor.

2-chronicles-6:41:10.summary: “You will be called priests of the Lord” shares priestly language but not the clothing or rejoicing.

2-chronicles-6:41:11.summary: God asks “what place is My rest?” and what house can be built for Him, directly engaging God’s resting place in a temple.
2-chronicles-6:41:11.why: Prophetic perspective on God’s rest in a house.

2-chronicles-6:41:12.summary: Having “put on Christ” in baptism shares only the clothing metaphor.

2-chronicles-6:41:13.summary: Good things of grain and wine loosely relate to rejoicing in good things.

2-chronicles-6:41:14.summary: Worship by the Spirit and boasting in Christ has no specific link to the ark, priests clothed, or rejoicing.

2-chronicles-6:41:16.summary: Israel delighting in houses “full of every good thing” in God’s goodness loosely echoes rejoicing in good things.
2-chronicles-6:41:16.why: God’s goodness enjoyed by His people.

2-chronicles-6:41:17.summary: Priests carrying the ark whose feet “rest” in the Jordan share ark and priest imagery but a different event.
2-chronicles-6:41:17.why: Earlier movement of the ark with priests.

2-chronicles-6:41:18.summary: God crowning the year with richness is a loose link to sons rejoicing in good things.

2-chronicles-6:41:19.summary: Heavenly armies clothed in white fine linen share only the clothing image.

2-chronicles-6:41:20.summary: The shown verse about trumpets and Jericho’s walls does not mention the ark or rest; no real link.
2-chronicles-6:41:20.why: No meaningful connection in shown text.

2-chronicles-6:41:21.summary: Those dwelling in God’s courts are “filled with the good things of Thy house,” echoing rejoicing in good things at the temple.
2-chronicles-6:41:21.why: Joy in the good things of God’s house.

2-chronicles-6:41:22.summary: God puts on “a helmet of salvation” and righteousness; shared clothing-with-salvation image, but applied to God as warrior.

2-chronicles-6:41:23.summary: God makes His people joy and exults over Jerusalem; a general rejoicing theme.
2-chronicles-6:41:23.why: Joy of God’s people in Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-6:42:0.summary: “The holy and sure blessings of David” covenant parallels “Remember the mercies of David.”

2-chronicles-6:42:1.summary: “Remember David, Lord” matches Solomon’s plea; this psalm also contains the arise-to-rest prayer.
2-chronicles-6:42:1.why: Psalm parallel to Solomon’s closing petition.

2-chronicles-6:42:2.summary: Solomon’s anointing as king identifies the “anointed one” who prays.
2-chronicles-6:42:2.why: Shows who the anointed one is.

2-chronicles-6:42:3.summary: God’s “mercy” will be with David forever, the promised mercies Solomon invokes.

2-chronicles-6:42:4.summary: “For ever I will keep My mercy for him” is the Davidic mercy Solomon asks God to remember.

2-chronicles-6:42:5.summary: “Do not turn away your face” is a verbal echo in an unrelated request to Bathsheba.

2-chronicles-6:42:6.summary: “His anointed” the Davidic king is named, but the context of nations’ rebellion differs.

2-chronicles-6:42:7.summary: The speaker is anointed by the Lord; shares only the anointing idea.

2-chronicles-6:42:9.summary: “The holy and sure blessings of David” applies David’s mercies to the risen Christ.
2-chronicles-6:42:9.why: NT fulfillment of the mercies of David.

2-chronicles-6:14:8.summary: Jeremiah 10:6 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
2-chronicles-6:14:8.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
2-chronicles-6:14:8.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

2-chronicles-6:14:17.summary: 1 Kings 6:12 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
2-chronicles-6:14:17.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
2-chronicles-6:14:17.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

2-chronicles-6:33:1.summary: Jeremiah 10:7 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
2-chronicles-6:33:1.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
2-chronicles-6:33:1.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

2-chronicles-7:1:2.summary: God answered David “with fire from heaven” that “consumed the whole burnt offering,” on the future temple site.
2-chronicles-7:1:2.why: Earlier divine fire at the same place.

2-chronicles-7:1:11.summary: Kings’ account of the dedication: “the Lord’s glory filled the house.”
2-chronicles-7:1:11.why: Parallel record of the same event.

2-chronicles-7:1:22.summary: Explicitly recalls that Solomon prayed and “the fire came down and consumed the whole burnt offerings.”
2-chronicles-7:1:22.why: Later retelling of this exact event.

2-chronicles-7:1:0.summary: Fire fell “from heaven and consumed the burnt offering” at Elijah’s prayer, a close parallel sign.

2-chronicles-7:1:3.summary: Elijah proposes the God who “answers by fire” is God; sets up the parallel but lacks the event itself.

2-chronicles-7:1:4.summary: Ezekiel sees “the house was full of the glory of the Lord,” echoing the glory filling the house.
2-chronicles-7:1:4.why: Glory returns to the visionary temple.

2-chronicles-7:1:5.summary: “The house of the Lord was full of glory” and Ezekiel falls on his face, echoing this scene.

2-chronicles-7:1:6.summary: The Lord coming to His sanctuary like a smelting fire is a loose fire-and-temple link.
2-chronicles-7:1:6.why: Future coming of the Lord to His temple.

2-chronicles-7:1:7.summary: A flame and torches pass between Abraham’s sacrifice pieces; loose divine fire with offerings.
2-chronicles-7:1:7.why: Early theophany by fire at a sacrifice.

2-chronicles-7:1:8.summary: At the tabernacle’s completion “the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord,” paralleling the temple dedication.

2-chronicles-7:1:9.summary: Same dedication: the house was filled with the Lord’s glory and the priests could not minister.
2-chronicles-7:1:9.why: Immediate context of the same event.

2-chronicles-7:1:10.summary: An earthquake during Paul and Silas’s prayer lacks fire, glory, or temple; only prayer answered dramatically.

2-chronicles-7:1:12.summary: “When Solomon finished praying all this prayer” is the Kings parallel to this moment.
2-chronicles-7:1:12.why: Kings’ account of what followed the prayer.

2-chronicles-7:1:13.summary: Fire from the rock consumes Gideon’s offering; a similar sign of divine fire on an offering.

2-chronicles-7:1:14.summary: God will be sanctified “in My glory” at the tabernacle; general promise of glory in the sanctuary.
2-chronicles-7:1:14.why: Promise of glory in the sanctuary.

2-chronicles-7:1:15.summary: Isaiah sees “the house was full of His glory” and filled with smoke.
2-chronicles-7:1:15.why: Vision of glory filling the temple.

2-chronicles-7:1:16.summary: God answers while they are still speaking; loosely matches the immediate answer to Solomon’s prayer.

2-chronicles-7:1:17.summary: God’s glory illuminating the heavenly city loosely parallels glory filling the house.

2-chronicles-7:1:18.summary: After prayer the place is shaken and filled with the Spirit; a loose parallel of divine response to prayer.

2-chronicles-7:1:19.summary: “The cloud filled the house” and the court filled with “the Lord’s glory,” though here the glory departs.

2-chronicles-7:1:20.summary: Daniel is answered while still speaking in prayer; loose prayer-answered parallel.

2-chronicles-7:1:21.summary: “I will fill this house with glory” promises glory for the second temple, echoing glory filling Solomon’s house.
2-chronicles-7:1:21.why: Promise of greater glory for a later temple.

2-chronicles-7:2:0.summary: The temple filled with smoke from God’s glory so “no one was able to enter,” as the priests could not enter.
2-chronicles-7:2:0.why: Heavenly echo of the inaccessible glory.

2-chronicles-7:2:1.summary: “The priests could not stand to minister… for the Lord’s glory filled God’s house.”

2-chronicles-7:2:2.summary: The Lord’s glory appeared like blazing fire on Sinai; general glory imagery.

2-chronicles-7:2:3.summary: Isaiah’s terror at seeing the Lord in the temple loosely parallels priests unable to enter.

2-chronicles-7:3:0.summary: The same praise “for it is good, for His mercy endures for ever” sung at the dedication.
2-chronicles-7:3:0.why: Same refrain at the same event.

2-chronicles-7:3:1.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord, for His mercy is for ever” repeats the liturgical refrain.
2-chronicles-7:3:1.why: Same refrain used later in battle.

2-chronicles-7:3:2.summary: Mary’s “His mercy is for generations” echoes enduring mercy generally.

2-chronicles-7:3:3.summary: Christ’s permanent priesthood has no specific link to the fire, glory, or mercy refrain.

2-chronicles-7:3:4.summary: Remembering the Lord’s mercy and goodness toward Israel loosely matches the praise theme.

2-chronicles-7:3:5.summary: “For it is good, for His mercy toward Israel endures for ever” at the second temple’s founding.
2-chronicles-7:3:5.why: Same refrain at the rebuilt temple.

2-chronicles-7:3:6.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord… for His mercy is for ever” is the psalm refrain behind this praise.

2-chronicles-7:3:7.summary: The people bowed down and worshipped when God visited them; a general worship response.
2-chronicles-7:3:7.why: Worship in response to God’s act.

2-chronicles-7:3:8.summary: Singers appointed “to praise the Lord, for His mercy endures for ever.”

2-chronicles-7:3:9.summary: Moses and Aaron fell on their faces in intercession; shared posture but different occasion.
2-chronicles-7:3:9.why: Falling on the face before God.

2-chronicles-7:3:10.summary: “Give thanks… for the Lord is good; His mercy is for ever” and gifts in the Lord’s house.
2-chronicles-7:3:10.why: Refrain promised for restored temple worship.

2-chronicles-7:3:11.summary: A call to bow down and fall before the Lord; general worship posture.

2-chronicles-7:3:12.summary: The assembly prostrated and blessed the Lord at David’s gathering; general worship parallel.

2-chronicles-7:3:14.summary: Moses and Aaron fell on their faces; only shared posture.

2-chronicles-7:3:15.summary: After fire fell from heaven, “all the people fell on their faces” confessing the Lord, closely parallel to this response.

2-chronicles-7:3:16.summary: “The Lord’s mercy is from eternity to eternity” echoes enduring mercy without the liturgical formula.

2-chronicles-7:3:17.summary: All the people “fell facedown upon the earth to worship” at the temple service, a close parallel scene.
2-chronicles-7:3:17.why: Similar communal worship at the temple.

2-chronicles-7:5:0.summary: The later “feast of Dedication” in Jerusalem shares the idea of dedicating the temple, but a different occasion.

2-chronicles-7:5:1.summary: The ruler provides sacrifices at festivals in Ezekiel’s temple; general royal provision of offerings.

2-chronicles-7:5:2.summary: Hezekiah and rulers give thousands of calves and sheep at a great feast, a royal mass sacrifice like Solomon’s.

2-chronicles-7:5:3.summary: Josiah supplies thousands of sheep and calves from the king’s property for the people, paralleling royal mass offerings.

2-chronicles-7:5:4.summary: Solomon and the congregation sacrifice calves and sheep beyond number at the same temple dedication.

2-chronicles-7:5:5.summary: Rulers present gifts “for the dedication of the altar,” a tabernacle precedent for dedication offerings.

2-chronicles-7:5:7.summary: Solomon plans the house to consecrate it with offerings; background to the dedication, not the event.

2-chronicles-7:5:8.summary: Micah asks whether thousands of rams please God, a contrast to large-scale sacrifice.
2-chronicles-7:5:8.why: Questions the value of sheer numbers.

2-chronicles-7:5:9.summary: Asa sacrifices seven hundred calves and seven thousand sheep; a similar royal sacrifice, different occasion.

2-chronicles-7:5:10.summary: Hezekiah’s assembly brings burnt offerings and consecrated calves and sheep; general sacrifice counts.

2-chronicles-7:5:11.summary: Solomon offers a “thousandfold whole burnt offering,” another lavish sacrifice by the same king.

2-chronicles-7:5:12.summary: David sacrifices a thousand calves, rams, and lambs for all Israel; similar mass offering at a related occasion.

2-chronicles-7:5:13.summary: The returned exiles “celebrated the dedication of God’s house” with sacrifices, a direct counterpart to Solomon’s dedication.

2-chronicles-7:6:19.summary: “Give thanks unto the Lord… for His mercy endures for ever” is the refrain the Levites sang.

2-chronicles-7:6:1.summary: Same occasion and refrain: “For it is good, for His mercy endures for ever.”

2-chronicles-7:6:2.summary: David appointed Levite psalm singers with instruments, the origin of the Levites’ “instruments… belonging to King David.”

2-chronicles-7:6:3.summary: God’s people knowing His name has no link to priests, Levites, or instruments.

2-chronicles-7:6:4.summary: Levites appointed to give thanks with instruments and priests sounding trumpets before the ark, the same arrangement.

2-chronicles-7:6:5.summary: A line on dwelling like those who rejoice has no specific link to the Levites’ music.

2-chronicles-7:6:7.summary: Hezekiah stations Levites with instruments “according to the command of King David,” continuing this order.

2-chronicles-7:6:8.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy is for ever” matches the sung refrain.

2-chronicles-7:6:9.summary: The law of the silver trumpets blown by priests gives background to priests sounding trumpets.

2-chronicles-7:6:10.summary: Amos condemns idle music-making; no meaningful link to the Levites’ temple praise.

2-chronicles-7:6:11.summary: David divides Aaron’s sons into divisions, background for priests standing “at their watches.”

2-chronicles-7:6:12.summary: “Thy mercy is for ever” echoes the refrain in a personal prayer.

2-chronicles-7:6:13.summary: David appointed singers who ministered “until Solomon built the Lord’s house,” leading into this scene.

2-chronicles-7:6:14.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; His mercy is for ever” repeats the refrain.

2-chronicles-7:6:15.summary: David appoints Asaph, Aiman, and Idithon’s sons with instruments for thanksgiving and praise.

2-chronicles-7:6:16.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; His mercy is for ever” repeats the refrain.

2-chronicles-7:6:17.summary: Singers chosen “to praise the Lord, for His mercy endures for ever,” with trumpets and instruments for God’s songs.

2-chronicles-7:6:18.summary: Priests “sounded trumpets before God’s ark,” the same priestly role.

2-chronicles-7:6:20.summary: David and Israel play before God with instruments and trumpets; general music in worship.

2-chronicles-7:7:0.summary: Hebrews’ altar and sacrifice outside the camp do not relate to sanctifying the court for excess offerings.

2-chronicles-7:7:2.summary: Defiling the Lord’s house is a distant contrast to sanctifying the court; no specific link.

2-chronicles-7:7:3.summary: Bronze fire pans become a covering for the altar; shares only the bronze altar motif.

2-chronicles-7:7:4.summary: Describes the “bronze altar” Solomon made, which proved too small for the offerings.

2-chronicles-7:8:0.summary: The promised land runs “from the river of Egypt,” matching the assembly’s extent to Egypt’s torrent.
2-chronicles-7:8:0.why: Shows fulfillment of the land promise.

2-chronicles-7:8:2.summary: Future nations keep the Festival of Tent-Pitching in Jerusalem; links to the feast but a different context.

2-chronicles-7:8:3.summary: Law commands the Feast of Tents for “seven days” at the chosen place, the feast Solomon kept.
2-chronicles-7:8:3.why: Torah basis for the seven-day feast.

2-chronicles-7:8:4.summary: Solomon ruled to Egypt’s borders; matches the realm’s extent but not the feast.

2-chronicles-7:8:5.summary: Land facing Egypt to “the entrance of Hamath” matches the boundary from Aimath to Egypt’s torrent.

2-chronicles-7:8:6.summary: Mentions the feast of Booths, the same festival, in a much later setting.

2-chronicles-7:8:7.summary: Post-exilic Israel keeps the feast of tents in the seventh month; a later observance of the same feast.

2-chronicles-7:8:8.summary: Prescribes the seventh-month “festival unto the Lord for seven days” with many offerings, the feast Solomon kept.

2-chronicles-7:8:9.summary: Jesus teaches in the temple during the feast of Booths; shown text only loosely related to Solomon’s feast.
2-chronicles-7:8:9.why: NT setting at the same feast.

2-chronicles-7:8:10.summary: “A very great assembly” gathers in Jerusalem for a feast, echoing the same phrase.

2-chronicles-7:8:11.summary: Israel’s boundaries from the Wadi of Egypt to “the entrance into Hamath” match the assembly’s range.

2-chronicles-7:8:12.summary: The Feast of Tents for seven days with an eighth-day closing observance matches Solomon’s feast.

2-chronicles-7:8:13.summary: Emath and the Wadi of the West mark Israel’s boundaries in a judgment oracle; place-name overlap only.
2-chronicles-7:8:13.why: Same border markers reversed in judgment.

2-chronicles-7:8:14.summary: States “Solomon also observed the eight days,” directly recalling this feast.
2-chronicles-7:8:14.why: Later retelling of the same feast.

2-chronicles-7:9:0.summary: Seven days of offerings then “the eighth day… a closing observance” matches the eighth-day celebration.
2-chronicles-7:9:0.why: Legal basis for the eighth day.

2-chronicles-7:9:1.summary: Joel’s call to a fast and lament has no real link to the dedication’s closing celebration.

2-chronicles-7:9:2.summary: Hezekiah’s assembly keeps “another seven days,” consciously modeled on extended festival celebration.

2-chronicles-7:9:3.summary: A concluding feast after six days of unleavened bread; similar closing-day pattern for a different feast.

2-chronicles-7:9:4.summary: “Seven days, and on the eighth day there was a closing observance” matches exactly.

2-chronicles-7:9:6.summary: The Maccabees celebrate “the altar’s dedication” for eight days, echoing Solomon’s dedication feast.
2-chronicles-7:9:6.why: Later altar dedication modeled on this.

2-chronicles-7:10:1.summary: Serving the Lord with gladness is a general joy-in-worship theme.

2-chronicles-7:10:2.summary: Solomon prayed “let Thy sons rejoice in good things”; the people go home rejoicing over good things.

2-chronicles-7:10:3.summary: “Rejoice before the Lord” at the chosen place, as the people rejoiced after the feast.

2-chronicles-7:10:4.summary: Let the heart of seekers rejoice; general joy theme.

2-chronicles-7:10:5.summary: A call to rejoice and exult in the Lord; general joy theme.

2-chronicles-7:10:6.summary: Israel shall “rejoice before the Lord” with household and Levite, the joy commanded at the chosen place.

2-chronicles-7:10:7.summary: Eat and rejoice before the Lord because He blessed you; general festal joy.

2-chronicles-7:10:8.summary: “All that the Lord had done for Israel His own people” echoes the good things done for Israel.

2-chronicles-7:10:9.summary: Rejoicing before the Lord at the chosen place; general festal joy.

2-chronicles-7:10:10.summary: The jailer rejoicing with his household after believing has no specific tie to the feast’s end.

2-chronicles-7:10:11.summary: Hezekiah’s festival is compared with “the days of Solomon,” referring back to this celebration.

2-chronicles-7:10:12.summary: Hezekiah and the people rejoiced at what God prepared; general joy after temple restoration.

2-chronicles-7:10:13.summary: Believers share food with gladness and simplicity of heart; loose echo of a glad heart.

2-chronicles-7:10:14.summary: God gladdened the psalmist by His works; general joy at God’s deeds.
2-chronicles-7:10:14.why: Joy at what God has done.

2-chronicles-7:10:15.summary: “Rejoice in your feast” refers to the Feast of Tents, exactly the occasion here.
2-chronicles-7:10:15.why: Command for joy at this feast.

2-chronicles-7:10:16.summary: Nehemiah sends people to feast for a holy day; general festal joy.

2-chronicles-7:10:17.summary: A general exhortation to rejoice has no specific link to this event.

2-chronicles-7:10:18.summary: Rejoicing in the goodness of God’s nation loosely matches joy over good things done for Israel.
2-chronicles-7:10:18.why: Joy in God’s goodness to His people.

2-chronicles-7:11:1.summary: Solomon resolved to build “a house for the Lord’s name and a house for his kingdom,” the two now completed.

2-chronicles-7:11:2.summary: Solomon-like speaker denies nothing his heart desired, then finds his works futile; loose contrast to prosperity.

2-chronicles-7:11:3.summary: “I built houses for myself” loosely parallels Solomon’s building projects.

2-chronicles-7:12:0.summary: The Lord appeared to Abram; shares only the theophany formula.

2-chronicles-7:12:1.summary: Same speech: “I have chosen and sanctified this house for My name.”

2-chronicles-7:12:2.summary: God “appeared to Solomon” at night earlier at Gibeon, the first such appearance.

2-chronicles-7:12:4.summary: Confidence that God hears requests; general answered-prayer theme.

2-chronicles-7:12:5.summary: The place God chooses for His name to receive burnt offerings and sacrifices, now designated “a house of sacrifice.”

2-chronicles-7:12:6.summary: “Your petition has been heard” echoes God’s assurance in a different setting.

2-chronicles-7:12:7.summary: “Your prayer has been heard” echoes God’s words to Solomon in a different setting.

2-chronicles-7:12:8.summary: God tells Hezekiah “I have heard your prayer,” in a temple context, echoing the same formula.
2-chronicles-7:12:8.why: Same divine answer to a king.

2-chronicles-7:12:9.summary: The Lord heard the needy’s desire; general answered-prayer theme.

2-chronicles-7:12:10.summary: Elijah and Elisha’s journey to the Jordan has no connection to God’s answer to Solomon.

2-chronicles-7:12:11.summary: God “chose… Mount Zion” and built His sanctuary there, matching His choosing this place.
2-chronicles-7:12:11.why: God’s choice of Zion for His sanctuary.

2-chronicles-7:12:12.summary: “God heard me; He attended to… my petition”; general answered prayer.

2-chronicles-7:12:13.summary: The place the Lord “shall choose” to set His name, where offerings are brought, now chosen as a house of sacrifice.

2-chronicles-7:12:14.summary: “The Lord chose Zion… as His dwelling,” paralleling “chosen this place for Myself.”

2-chronicles-7:13:1.summary: God will “shut up heaven, so that there is no rain” as covenant judgment, the same threat.

2-chronicles-7:13:2.summary: The witnesses “shut heaven, so that rain may not fall”; shared drought wording in a different setting.

2-chronicles-7:13:3.summary: Christ who opens and shuts with David’s key shares only the word “shut,” not drought.

2-chronicles-7:13:4.summary: Famine and “death in your land” sent by God upon Israel matches God sending death among His people.

2-chronicles-7:13:5.summary: Locusts devour every tree in Egypt; shares the locust-devouring image but on Egypt.

2-chronicles-7:13:6.summary: God shuts people in and none can open; only the idea of God shutting.

2-chronicles-7:13:7.summary: God sent the locust that “devoured” as His force among His people and promises restoration, matching locust judgment and healing.

2-chronicles-7:13:8.summary: God sends “death” and famine against a land; similar list of judgments.

2-chronicles-7:13:9.summary: An outbreak strikes the people and is stopped by atonement; loose plague-and-atonement parallel.

2-chronicles-7:13:10.summary: God spoke and locusts came, recalling the Egyptian plague.

2-chronicles-7:13:11.summary: Locusts devour and lay waste vine and fig trees in Judah, a realization of the locust devouring the tree.

2-chronicles-7:13:12.summary: “Heaven was shut” in Elijah’s day bringing famine, an instance of this judgment.

2-chronicles-7:13:13.summary: God overturning all without challenge is a general sovereignty statement, not drought, locust, or death.

2-chronicles-7:13:14.summary: God threatens to strike Israel “with death”; loosely matches sending death among His people.

2-chronicles-7:13:15.summary: A fruitful land turned to brine for wickedness; loose land-judgment theme.

2-chronicles-7:14:0.summary: “Let us return to the Lord” and lift hearts to God “in heaven” match turning and praying for God to hear from heaven.

2-chronicles-7:14:1.summary: Seek God, forsake wicked “ways,” return, and He “will abundantly forgive your sins,” paralleling seek, turn, and forgiveness.
2-chronicles-7:14:1.why: Same sequence of seeking, turning, and pardon.

2-chronicles-7:14:2.summary: “Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you” echoes humbling oneself, though the Greek-based text says “ashamed.”

2-chronicles-7:14:3.summary: Not covering impiety but confessing leads to favor; general confession theme.

2-chronicles-7:14:4.summary: Solomon’s petition that God “hear from heaven” and “be propitious” toward repentant sinners is answered here almost verbatim.

2-chronicles-7:14:5.summary: Seeking the Lord with all the heart in distress and returning to Him matches seeking God’s face and turning.

2-chronicles-7:14:6.summary: God promises “I listen, heal her,” matching hearing and healing the land.

2-chronicles-7:14:7.summary: Manasseh “sought the face of the Lord,” humbled himself, prayed, and God heard, enacting this promise.

2-chronicles-7:14:8.summary: God desires the impious to “turn from his way and live,” matching turning from wicked ways.

2-chronicles-7:14:10.summary: Israel confesses sins and their heart “will feel shame,” paralleling being ashamed and turning to God.
2-chronicles-7:14:10.why: Covenant basis for shame and confession.

2-chronicles-7:14:11.summary: The lawless one who “turns from the lawlessness” lives; call to “turn back” from impieties.
2-chronicles-7:14:11.why: Prophetic teaching on turning from wickedness.

2-chronicles-7:14:12.summary: Jeremiah laments no healing for his people; a contrast with the promise to heal the land.

2-chronicles-7:14:13.summary: “Thy name had not been called upon us” echoes “My people, upon whom My name has been invoked,” in a lament.

2-chronicles-7:14:14.summary: Returning with all the heart leads God to “heal your sins” and restore, matching repentance and healing.
2-chronicles-7:14:14.why: Covenant promise of healing on return.

2-chronicles-7:14:15.summary: The deliverer turns ungodliness away from Jacob; loose forgiveness theme.

2-chronicles-7:14:16.summary: “Then hear from heaven… and be propitious” is Solomon’s request, which God promises here.

2-chronicles-7:14:17.summary: God did not tell Jacob to seek in vain; loose link to seeking His face.

2-chronicles-7:14:18.summary: Saul praying in Damascus shares only the words “seek” and “praying,” no real connection.

2-chronicles-7:14:19.summary: Babylon could not be healed; only the word “healed,” in judgment on a foreign nation.

2-chronicles-7:14:20.summary: Records Manasseh’s prayer and “how He listened to him” before his turning back, an example of this promise.
2-chronicles-7:14:20.why: Documented case of God hearing repentance.

2-chronicles-7:14:21.summary: A plea that God “heal” the shaken land’s fractures; partial echo of healing the land.
2-chronicles-7:14:21.why: Prayer for healing of the land.

2-chronicles-7:14:22.summary: A wish that God “hear your petitions” and be reconciled; general hearing and reconciliation.

2-chronicles-7:15:6.summary: “Let Thine ears be attentive to the voice of my petition” echoes ears attentive to prayer.

2-chronicles-7:15:0.summary: “The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears attend to their petition” echoes eyes and ears to prayer.
2-chronicles-7:15:0.why: NT echo of the eyes-and-ears motif.

2-chronicles-7:15:2.summary: Solomon asked “Let Thine eyes be open toward this house… to hear the prayer,” which God now grants.

2-chronicles-7:15:3.summary: “Let Thine ear be attentive and Thine eyes opened to hear” repeats the same formula.

2-chronicles-7:15:4.summary: “Hear my prayer” is a general plea; no eyes or place language.

2-chronicles-7:15:5.summary: “The eyes of the Lord… are always upon” the land; shared image of God’s watchful eyes.

2-chronicles-7:15:7.summary: “Thou didst choose this house… to be a house of prayer and petition,” recalling God’s commitment to prayer here.
2-chronicles-7:15:7.why: Later appeal to the temple’s role.

2-chronicles-7:16:0.summary: Same speech: “My eyes will be open,” continued in “My eyes and My heart will be there.”

2-chronicles-7:16:1.summary: Same speech: God has “chosen this place for Myself,” repeated as chosen and sanctified this house.

2-chronicles-7:16:2.summary: God “chose Jerusalem for My name to be there,” the same choice confirmed for the house.

2-chronicles-7:16:4.summary: Solomon asked God’s eyes be open toward this house where His name is invoked; God confirms His eyes will be there.

2-chronicles-7:16:5.summary: Jesus speaks of His body as the sanctuary; a typological link to God’s dwelling in the house.

2-chronicles-7:16:6.summary: All the fullness of deity dwells in Christ bodily; loose typological dwelling theme.

2-chronicles-7:16:7.summary: “Here I will dwell, for I selected her… for age upon age” parallels chosen for His name “for ever.”

2-chronicles-7:16:8.summary: Manasseh defiles the house of which God said “My name shall be in Jerusalem for ever,” quoting this promise.

2-chronicles-7:16:9.summary: The Lord “who chose Jerusalem” rebukes the slanderer; shared election theme only.

2-chronicles-7:16:10.summary: Refers to the place God shall choose for His name; background rule rather than a parallel.

2-chronicles-7:16:11.summary: “I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there” parallels choosing the house for His name.

2-chronicles-7:16:12.summary: The voice at Jesus’ baptism has no link to God choosing the temple.

2-chronicles-7:16:13.summary: Refers to “the city Thou didst choose and the house I built for Thy name”; a repeated phrase in Solomon’s prayer.

2-chronicles-7:16:14.summary: Repeats “the city Thou didst choose, and the house I have built for Thy name” in the exile petition.

2-chronicles-7:16:15.summary: Rejoicing at “the place which the Lord… shall choose for His name”; background to God’s choice.
2-chronicles-7:16:15.why: Deuteronomic anticipation of the chosen place.

2-chronicles-7:16:16.summary: Quotes God to Solomon: “In this house… I shall place My name there for ever,” in Manasseh’s defilement.

2-chronicles-7:16:17.summary: Solomon’s petition about drought and praying toward this place; relates more to 7:13–14 than to choosing the house.

2-chronicles-7:16:18.summary: Manasseh builds an altar in the house where God said “In Jerusalem I shall place My name.”

2-chronicles-7:17:9.summary: “If you walk in My way… as your father David walked” is the same conditional charge to Solomon.
2-chronicles-7:17:9.why: Earlier form of the same condition.

2-chronicles-7:17:12.summary: David charges Solomon to walk in God’s ways keeping His commandments, statutes, and judgments.

2-chronicles-7:17:0.summary: God will cause His people “to walk in My ordinances, keep My judgments”; shared phrasing in a new-covenant promise.

2-chronicles-7:17:1.summary: Jeroboam gets the same condition: walk, keep “commandments and ordinances as David… did,” and a house will be built.
2-chronicles-7:17:1.why: Same conditional formula to another king.

2-chronicles-7:17:2.summary: “If you walk in My ways and keep My commands” to the high priest; shared conditional formula, different person.

2-chronicles-7:17:3.summary: Keep His ordinances and commandments that it may be well; general covenant obedience.

2-chronicles-7:17:4.summary: Blessings promised for keeping all His commandments; general conditional covenant blessing.

2-chronicles-7:17:5.summary: “If you keep My commandments” in Jesus’ teaching; shares only the conditional obedience idea.

2-chronicles-7:17:6.summary: Solomon recalls the promise of a man on David’s throne if sons walk “as you have walked,” which God reaffirms here.

2-chronicles-7:17:7.summary: So that they might keep His ordinances; general obedience theme.

2-chronicles-7:17:8.summary: David charges Solomon to serve God wholeheartedly, warning He will forsake him if forsaken; same conditional covenant.

2-chronicles-7:17:10.summary: Keeping Jesus’ commandments shows love; shares only the obedience theme.

2-chronicles-7:18:0.summary: “You shall never lack a man before Me sitting upon the throne of Israel” matches the covenant promise God affirms.

2-chronicles-7:18:2.summary: Nathan’s oracle that God will “set his throne upright for ever” is the covenant with David referenced.

2-chronicles-7:18:3.summary: God swore to set David’s fruit on his throne if his sons keep His covenant, the same conditional promise.

2-chronicles-7:18:6.summary: God establishes David’s seed and throne, with discipline if sons abandon His law; same covenant terms.

2-chronicles-7:19:0.summary: If Israel does not keep His commandments, curses come; the covenant warning behind this conditional.

2-chronicles-7:19:1.summary: “If you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances” introduces covenant curses; general conditional.

2-chronicles-7:19:2.summary: God will scatter Israel among the nations and desolate the land for disobedience, the threat that follows here.

2-chronicles-7:19:3.summary: Solomon later turned after other gods and built high places, fulfilling the very warning given him.

2-chronicles-7:19:5.summary: “If you forsake Him, He will forsake you utterly” warns Solomon in parallel terms.

2-chronicles-7:19:6.summary: Disobedience leads to exile where “you shall serve other gods” and become “a parable,” matching 7:19–20.

2-chronicles-7:19:7.summary: If people and king do evil they will be swept away; general conditional warning.
2-chronicles-7:19:7.why: Similar warning to king and people.

2-chronicles-7:19:8.summary: Making idols and doing evil will cause Israel to “perish from the land,” matching the warning against other gods.

2-chronicles-7:19:9.summary: If Israel goes and serves “other gods and bow[s] down to them,” God will destroy them from the land.
2-chronicles-7:19:9.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

2-chronicles-7:20:1.summary: “A parable, and a tale among all the nations” is the exact curse phrase.

2-chronicles-7:20:0.summary: God “cast them from His presence” for rejecting Him, fulfilling the threat of removal.

2-chronicles-7:20:3.summary: Scattered Judah becomes “a reproach, a parable” in every place, echoing the curse.
2-chronicles-7:20:3.why: Prophetic use of the same curse.

2-chronicles-7:20:4.summary: “The Lord removed them from their land in wrath,” matching “I will remove you from the land.”

2-chronicles-7:20:6.summary: God tears down what He built and plucks up what He planted; loose judgment theme.

2-chronicles-7:20:7.summary: Passers-by hiss and mock ruined Jerusalem, fulfilling its becoming a byword among nations.

2-chronicles-7:20:8.summary: “Thou madest us a parable among the nations,” the same curse lamented.

2-chronicles-7:20:9.summary: God watched to tear down and will build; loose judgment-and-restoration theme.
