2-chronicles-29:12:4.summary: Levites listed by “Kaath’s sons”, “Merari’s sons”, and Gersam’s sons; same three-clan list format.

2-chronicles-29:12:5.summary: Merari line “son of Kisai son of Abdi”, matching “Kis son of Abdi” from Merari’s sons.

2-chronicles-29:12:6.summary: Genealogy of Levi’s sons Gershon, Kohath, Merari; general clan background.

2-chronicles-29:12:7.summary: Levite divisions including Kaath’s sons and a “Joel”; general clan genealogy.

2-chronicles-29:12:8.summary: Census and duties of Kohath’s sons; clan background only.

2-chronicles-29:13:0.summary: Introduces Asaph son of Barachia, ancestor of “Asaph’s sons” here.

2-chronicles-29:13:1.summary: “From Elisaphan’s sons” — same Levite subclan named in the source.

2-chronicles-29:13:3.summary: Asaph son of Barachia appointed among Levite singers; identifies Asaph’s line.

2-chronicles-29:13:4.summary: Elzaphan son of Uzziel is the ancestor of “Elisaphan’s sons.”

2-chronicles-29:14:0.summary: Introduces “Heman the psalm singer”, ancestor of “Heman’s sons.”

2-chronicles-29:14:1.summary: Sons of Asaph, Aiman, and Idithon appointed—the Heman and Jeduthun guilds named here.

2-chronicles-29:14:2.summary: Idithon’s sons include “Semei”; same Jeduthun guild and a matching name.

2-chronicles-29:14:3.summary: Singers under Asaph, Idithon, and Aiman; same musical guilds.

2-chronicles-29:14:4.summary: Aiman, Asaph, and Aithan sound cymbals; related guild leaders, Jeduthun not explicitly named.

2-chronicles-29:15:0.summary: Judah carries out “the king’s and the rulers’ ordinance according to the Lord’s word”; parallels obeying the king’s command by the Lord’s ordinance.
2-chronicles-29:15:0.why: Same pattern of royal command backed by God’s word.

2-chronicles-29:15:2.summary: Hezekiah’s command to “purify yourselves and purify the house”, which this verse fulfills.

2-chronicles-29:15:3.summary: Judas chose blameless priests to purify the temple; later parallel temple cleansing.

2-chronicles-29:16:0.summary: Asa burned an idol “in the Kedron torrent”; same place used for disposing of defilement.
2-chronicles-29:16:0.why: Kedron as the dump for impurity.

2-chronicles-29:16:1.summary: Copies of heavenly things “cleansed” with sacrifices; typological link to cleansing the sanctuary.

2-chronicles-29:16:2.summary: Jesus “cast out” traders from the temple; general temple-cleansing parallel.

2-chronicles-29:16:4.summary: Describes the tent’s holy places where priests enter; background on inner sanctuary.

2-chronicles-29:16:5.summary: Veil dividing Holy Place from Holy of Holies; background on the inner parts priests entered.

2-chronicles-29:16:6.summary: Jesus crosses “the winter-stream Kidron”; same place, unrelated event.

2-chronicles-29:16:7.summary: David crosses “the Kidron torrent”; same place, unrelated event.

2-chronicles-29:16:8.summary: Tombs “full of… all uncleanness”; shares the word uncleanness in a moral metaphor.

2-chronicles-29:16:9.summary: God will save from “all your uncleannesses”; general cleansing theme.

2-chronicles-29:16:10.summary: Describes the inner sanctuary of Solomon’s house; background to where priests went inside.

2-chronicles-29:16:11.summary: Construction of the Holy of Holies; background on the inner house.

2-chronicles-29:16:12.summary: Priests bring the ark into the Holy of Holies; only priests entered the inner house.
2-chronicles-29:16:12.why: Shows priestly access to inner sanctuary.

2-chronicles-29:16:13.summary: Maccabees “cleansed the holy places” and carried defiled stones to an unclean place; close parallel to carrying uncleanness out.

2-chronicles-29:17:0.summary: Hezekiah opened the temple doors “in the first month”; same reform and timing.

2-chronicles-29:17:1.summary: First month instituted with Passover on set days; calendar background, as Passover follows the cleansing.

2-chronicles-29:17:2.summary: Describes the temple porch; background on the area purified.

2-chronicles-29:17:3.summary: Describes the ailam (porch) before the house; background on structures entered.

2-chronicles-29:17:4.summary: David’s pattern for the temple’s rooms; general structural background.

2-chronicles-29:17:5.summary: The shut doors and extinguished lamps that this purification reversed.

2-chronicles-29:18:0.summary: Solomon made the golden lampstands and tables; background to temple furnishings purified.

2-chronicles-29:18:1.summary: Bread on “the pure table”, burnt offerings, and lampstand—the regular worship that the purified furnishings restore.
2-chronicles-29:18:1.why: Describes the service of these articles.

2-chronicles-29:18:2.summary: Solomon made the bronze altar; background to the altar of burnt offering purified.

2-chronicles-29:20:0.summary: Joshua “rose in the morning” for a sacred act; shared early-rising formula.

2-chronicles-29:20:1.summary: Moses “rose early” and built an altar; shares the early-rising formula before worship.

2-chronicles-29:20:2.summary: God sending prophets “from early morning”; idiom only, no real link.

2-chronicles-29:20:3.summary: Abraham “rose in the morning” to offer a burnt offering; shares early rising to sacrifice.

2-chronicles-29:21:0.summary: Law of the sin offering of a calf for the anointed priest; ritual background for the calves offered for sin.
2-chronicles-29:21:0.why: Levitical basis for the sin offerings.

2-chronicles-29:21:1.summary: “Seven calves and seven rams” offered for atonement for Job’s friends; shares the sevenfold offering.

2-chronicles-29:21:2.summary: “Seven calves and seven unblemished rams” plus a goat “for sin”; close parallel in offering composition.

2-chronicles-29:21:3.summary: Balak’s seven altars with a calf and ram each; pagan setting, only the number seven matches.

2-chronicles-29:21:4.summary: Balaam asks for “seven calves and seven rams”; verbal overlap but pagan context.

2-chronicles-29:21:5.summary: Levites bringing the ark “sacrificed seven calves and seven rams”; same offering at a temple-worship milestone.

2-chronicles-29:21:6.summary: Returned exiles offer bulls, rams, lambs and “male goats for sin” for all Israel; parallel restoration offering.

2-chronicles-29:21:7.summary: Balaam asks for “seven calves and seven rams”; verbal overlap only in a pagan context.

2-chronicles-29:21:8.summary: Congregation offers a calf and “one male goat for sin” for unintentional sin; legal basis for communal sin offering.
2-chronicles-29:21:8.why: Law behind the national sin offering.

2-chronicles-29:21:9.summary: Christ made “sin” on our behalf; typological fulfillment of sin offerings.

2-chronicles-29:22:0.summary: Priest pours out the blood at the altar’s base; same blood rite performed here.

2-chronicles-29:22:1.summary: Moses slaughtered the ram and “poured the blood all around against the altar”; same rite as here.

2-chronicles-29:22:2.summary: “Poured the blood all around against the altar” at the priests’ ordination; same rite.

2-chronicles-29:22:3.summary: Sin-offering calf’s blood poured at the altar, “cleansing the altar”; parallel to purifying sacrifices.

2-chronicles-29:22:4.summary: Pour out “all its blood beside the base of the altar”; legal pattern for the blood rite.
2-chronicles-29:22:4.why: Law of blood at the altar.

2-chronicles-29:22:5.summary: The calf’s blood poured beside the altar of burnt offerings; legal background to the rite.

2-chronicles-29:22:6.summary: “Almost everything is cleansed with blood”; theological reflection on blood purification.
2-chronicles-29:22:6.why: New Testament meaning of blood rites.

2-chronicles-29:23:1.summary: “Lay his hand upon the head of the offering” to make atonement; the rite performed on the goats.
2-chronicles-29:23:1.why: Explains the laying on of hands.

2-chronicles-29:24:0.summary: Offerings from “all Israel’s families… to make atonement”; shares atonement for all Israel.

2-chronicles-29:24:1.summary: Peace made “through the blood of His cross”; typological fulfillment of blood propitiation.

2-chronicles-29:24:2.summary: Priest offers burnt offering and “shall make atonement”; general atonement rite.

2-chronicles-29:24:3.summary: Blood put on the altar “to make atonement upon it”; parallels propitiation with blood at the altar.

2-chronicles-29:24:5.summary: Reconciled “through the death of His Son”; general reconciliation theme.

2-chronicles-29:24:6.summary: Seventy weeks for sin “to be wiped away”; broad atonement theme.

2-chronicles-29:24:7.summary: God “reconciling the world to Himself” in Christ; broad atonement parallel.

2-chronicles-29:24:8.summary: The ruler provides “offerings for sin… burnt offerings… to make atonement for the house of Israel”; close parallel to the king’s order.

2-chronicles-29:24:9.summary: Christ as high priest “to make propitiation for the sins of the people”; typological echo of propitiation.

2-chronicles-29:24:10.summary: Sin offerings whose blood makes atonement in the holy place; ritual background.

2-chronicles-29:25:4.summary: “Gad the prophet, David’s seer” — the same Gad named in the ordinance.

2-chronicles-29:25:13.summary: Names “Nathan the prophet” and “Gad the seer” with David; same figures.

2-chronicles-29:25:15.summary: “Gad, David’s seer”; same prophet named in the source.

2-chronicles-29:25:0.summary: Levites stationed “following David’s ordinance” and “the commands of David”; same basis for Levitical order.

2-chronicles-29:25:1.summary: Four thousand praised the Lord “with the instruments that he made”—David’s instruments for Levites.

2-chronicles-29:25:2.summary: Levitical psalm singers assigned divisions; general background on singers.

2-chronicles-29:25:3.summary: Singers stationed “according to the commands of David… the king’s prophets”; same Davidic-prophetic authority.
2-chronicles-29:25:3.why: Parallel appeal to David’s prophetic order.

2-chronicles-29:25:7.summary: David appoints Levites with instruments and cymbals to praise; origin of this musical order.

2-chronicles-29:25:8.summary: Trumpets, cymbals, and instruments for God’s songs; general background.

2-chronicles-29:25:9.summary: Carrying out the king’s ordinance “according to the Lord’s word”; similar royal-and-divine command pattern.
2-chronicles-29:25:9.why: Royal command backed by God’s word.

2-chronicles-29:25:10.summary: David’s divinely given pattern for the temple; loosely parallels a divine ordinance through David.

2-chronicles-29:25:11.summary: “Nathan the prophet” speaks to David; same prophet, different topic.

2-chronicles-29:25:12.summary: “Nathan the prophet” sent to David; same prophet, unrelated event.

2-chronicles-29:25:14.summary: David’s plan came “from the Lord’s hand”; supports the idea of divinely given ordinance.

2-chronicles-29:25:16.summary: David “stationed psalm singers before the altar”; same act attributed to David.

2-chronicles-29:26:0.summary: Levites praise with the instruments David made; explains “David’s instruments.”

2-chronicles-29:26:1.summary: Priests “sounded trumpets before God’s ark”; same division: priests with trumpets.

2-chronicles-29:26:2.summary: Amos condemns revelers with instruments; the Greek wording here lacks the David-instrument link.

2-chronicles-29:26:3.summary: Levites with cymbals, nablai and kinyrai with priests “sounding trumpets”; same arrangement at the temple dedication.

2-chronicles-29:26:4.summary: Priests sound sacred trumpets at Jericho; priests with trumpets, different setting.

2-chronicles-29:26:5.summary: Praise with trumpet, lyre, cymbals; general worship-with-instruments theme.

2-chronicles-29:26:6.summary: Hezekiah vows to bless God with a harp before God’s house; same king and musical worship.
2-chronicles-29:26:6.why: Hezekiah’s own devotion to temple song.

2-chronicles-29:26:7.summary: “Sound the trumpet” at the feast; general trumpet worship theme.

2-chronicles-29:26:8.summary: Blow trumpets “over your whole burnt offerings”; law behind priests sounding trumpets at sacrifice.
2-chronicles-29:26:8.why: Legal basis for trumpets at offerings.

2-chronicles-29:26:10.summary: The Greek wording speaks of a dwelling of rejoicing; no instruments or trumpets in the Saints text.
2-chronicles-29:26:10.why: Greek reading drops the musical link.

2-chronicles-29:26:11.summary: Priests “sounded trumpets continually before the ark”; same priestly trumpet role.

2-chronicles-29:26:12.summary: Music with lyre and “hammered trumpets”; general worship-instrument theme.

2-chronicles-29:27:0.summary: Burnt offerings “with rejoicing and songs according to David’s direction”; same pattern of offering with Davidic song.

2-chronicles-29:27:1.summary: People worship and praise at the temple’s dedication; general worship parallel.

2-chronicles-29:27:2.summary: Captives cannot sing the Lord’s song in a foreign land; only loose contrast with temple song.

2-chronicles-29:27:3.summary: “Give thanks to the Lord… His mercy is for ever”; typical temple song, not specified in source.

2-chronicles-29:27:4.summary: Jehoshaphat appoints singers to give praise; parallel royal ordering of song.

2-chronicles-29:27:5.summary: Aaron’s sons sound “hammered trumpets” during the offering; close parallel of trumpets with sacrifice.

2-chronicles-29:28:0.summary: People who know “the cry of triumph”; general joyful worship.

2-chronicles-29:28:1.summary: Processions with musicians in the holy place and assemblies blessing God; general worship parallel.

2-chronicles-29:28:2.summary: Elders fall down and sing a new song with lyres and incense; heavenly worship parallel.

2-chronicles-29:28:3.summary: “The psalm singers praised with their voices” during the sacrifice; close parallel to “the psalm singers sang.”

2-chronicles-29:29:0.summary: Jehoshaphat and all Judah bowed and worshiped; parallel king-and-people worship.

2-chronicles-29:29:1.summary: “Every knee should bend”; general bowing-in-worship theme.

2-chronicles-29:29:2.summary: “All kings will bow before him”; general bowing theme.

2-chronicles-29:29:4.summary: “Every knee will bend to Me”; general bowing theme.

2-chronicles-29:29:5.summary: All the people “fell facedown… to worship their Lord” after the offering; close liturgical parallel.

2-chronicles-29:30:0.summary: “Rejoice in the Lord always”; general rejoicing theme.

2-chronicles-29:30:1.summary: A song “of David” calling to exult and sing psalms; example of Davidic praise.

2-chronicles-29:30:2.summary: Psalm “Of David” calling to rejoice and exult; Davidic praise example.

2-chronicles-29:30:3.summary: David appointed praise “through Asaph and his brethren”; origin of hymning with words of David and Asaph.

2-chronicles-29:30:4.summary: “Let Israel rejoice”; general rejoicing in worship.

2-chronicles-29:30:5.summary: “Serve the Lord with gladness”; general joyful worship.

2-chronicles-29:30:6.summary: “Let us bow down and fall before Him”; matches hymning then falling down and worshiping.

2-chronicles-29:30:7.summary: David’s psalms spoken by “the Spirit of the Lord”; supports David’s words as prophetic hymns.

2-chronicles-29:31:0.summary: “Fill his hands” with a calf to become a priest; explains the consecration idiom “filled your hands.”

2-chronicles-29:31:1.summary: Everyone “whose heart approved” brought offerings; parallel to those “eager in heart.”

2-chronicles-29:31:2.summary: Everyone “who welcomes it in his heart” brings offerings; willing-heart giving.

2-chronicles-29:31:4.summary: Freewill offering for God’s house; general voluntary-offering theme.

2-chronicles-29:31:5.summary: Mentions “freewill offerings” to the Lord; general legal background.

2-chronicles-29:31:6.summary: Law of bringing whole burnt offerings; general background.

2-chronicles-29:32:1.summary: Burnt offerings of calves, rams, and lambs in large numbers; parallel national offering.

2-chronicles-29:32:0.summary: Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings; general large-offering parallel.

2-chronicles-29:32:2.summary: Dedication offering of bulls, rams, and lambs; close parallel in composition and occasion.

2-chronicles-29:32:3.summary: Solomon dedicates the house with vast offerings; general parallel.

2-chronicles-29:34:1.summary: “Enough priests had not purified themselves”; same shortage of purified priests under Hezekiah.

2-chronicles-29:34:2.summary: Levites cleansed to perform the Tent’s works; background on Levite purity.

2-chronicles-29:34:3.summary: Hezekiah commanded the Levites to purify themselves, which they did eagerly.

2-chronicles-29:34:4.summary: Levites sacrifice for those not purified; same pattern of Levites assisting during impurity.

2-chronicles-29:34:5.summary: Levites given to perform ministries while priests keep the altar; background on division of labor.

2-chronicles-29:34:6.summary: “Upright in heart” clinging to righteousness; no real link to Levites helping priests.

2-chronicles-29:34:7.summary: Levites shall not approach the altar; contrasts with Levites helping at sacrifices.

2-chronicles-29:34:8.summary: God saves the “upright in heart”; no link to the Levite episode in Greek text.

2-chronicles-29:34:9.summary: Levites given as a gift to Aaron to perform works; background for Levites assisting priests.

2-chronicles-29:34:10.summary: People “offer eagerly” in gladness; shares eagerness theme.

2-chronicles-29:34:11.summary: Psalmist washes hands and goes around the altar; no clear link to the Levites’ purification.

2-chronicles-29:35:0.summary: Fat placed on the altar; ritual background for the fat of offerings.

2-chronicles-29:35:1.summary: Drink offerings to accompany burnt offerings and sacrifices of deliverance; law behind the libations here.

2-chronicles-29:35:2.summary: “All the fat is the Lord’s” in peace offerings; background to the fat of salvation offerings.

2-chronicles-29:35:3.summary: Continual burnt offerings by David’s arrangement; general background of ordered service.

2-chronicles-29:35:4.summary: Jacob pours a drink offering on a pillar; incidental libation only.

2-chronicles-29:35:5.summary: Prescribes the drink offering with a sacrifice; legal libation background.

2-chronicles-29:35:6.summary: Priests and Levites stationed over the service of God; parallel to the work of the house set right.

2-chronicles-29:35:7.summary: “Let everything be done fittingly and in order”; general order-in-worship theme.

2-chronicles-29:36:0.summary: Sudden great response in a single day; loose parallel to sudden turn of the people.

2-chronicles-29:36:2.summary: Joy before God because of the people; general rejoicing theme.

2-chronicles-29:36:3.summary: People rejoice because “the Lord had made them joyful” in the house’s work; parallel divine-enabled rejoicing.

2-chronicles-29:36:5.summary: God attended to “the preparation of their heart”; loosely echoes God having prepared for the people.

2-chronicles-29:36:6.summary: David rejoices that the people “offer eagerly… in gladness” and asks God to direct their hearts; parallels joyful offering God enabled.

2-chronicles-29:36:7.summary: “The Lord’s hand gave them one heart”; same idea of God preparing the people under Hezekiah.
2-chronicles-29:36:7.why: Shows God’s work in the people’s hearts.

2-chronicles-29:8:4.summary: Jeremiah 29:18 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
2-chronicles-29:8:4.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
2-chronicles-29:8:4.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

2-chronicles-29:36:1.summary: Proverbs 16:1 has no corresponding passage in this edition, which follows the Greek text; there is no Saints reading to compare.
2-chronicles-29:36:1.why: Compare a Hebrew-based translation if this passage matters for study.
2-chronicles-29:36:1.note: Passage unavailable in this edition; the review records the absence rather than an interpretation.

2-chronicles-30:1:0.summary: “Christ, our Passover… let us keep the feast”; typological fulfillment of keeping Passover.

2-chronicles-30:1:1.summary: Prophetic charge against “Ephraim” mingled among peoples; background on Ephraim’s state.

2-chronicles-30:1:3.summary: Priests and Levites from all Israel gathered to Judah’s king; earlier northern-to-Jerusalem movement.
2-chronicles-30:1:3.why: Precedent for northern Israelites coming south.

2-chronicles-30:1:4.summary: Institution of the Passover for “the whole congregation”; the law Hezekiah invites Israel to keep.

2-chronicles-30:1:5.summary: “The Lord is not with Israel, all the sons of Ephraim”; background on Ephraim’s estrangement.

2-chronicles-30:1:6.summary: Runners went through “Ephraim and Manasse”; the response to this very invitation.
2-chronicles-30:1:6.why: Shows how the invitation was received.

2-chronicles-30:1:7.summary: God’s compassion for “Ephraim”; general appeal to Ephraim.

2-chronicles-30:1:8.summary: Israel did not return to their God; background to the call to return.

2-chronicles-30:1:9.summary: Those seeking the Lord from Israel’s tribes “came to Jerusalem to sacrifice”; parallel northern pilgrimage.
2-chronicles-30:1:9.why: Precedent of northerners worshipping in Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-30:1:10.summary: Josiah’s Passover preparations; parallel later Passover.

2-chronicles-30:2:1.summary: Proverb about a foolish king; no link to taking counsel for Passover.

2-chronicles-30:2:2.summary: “Deliverance is in much counsel”; general wisdom about counsel.

2-chronicles-30:2:3.summary: David “took counsel” with leaders and the whole assembly for a national religious act; parallel procedure.

2-chronicles-30:2:4.summary: A great assembly kept the feast “in the second month”; fulfillment of this decision.

2-chronicles-30:2:5.summary: Counsel remains with those who deliberate; general wisdom.

2-chronicles-30:2:6.summary: Passover sacrificed “on the fourteenth day of the second month”; carrying out this decision.

2-chronicles-30:3:0.summary: The priests were too few and slower to purify; same shortage of purified priests.
2-chronicles-30:3:0.why: Earlier evidence of the same problem.

2-chronicles-30:3:1.summary: Unleavened bread from the fourteenth of “the first month”; the regular time that could not be kept.

2-chronicles-30:3:2.summary: Passover kept on the fourteenth day; the appointed time missed.

2-chronicles-30:4:0.summary: “The whole assembly agreed… the matter was right in the eyes of all”; parallel approval formula.

2-chronicles-30:5:0.summary: All Israel gathered “from Dan to Beersheba”; the same full-extent formula.

2-chronicles-30:5:1.summary: Cyrus orders “a proclamation throughout his kingdom in writing”; parallel written proclamation.

2-chronicles-30:5:2.summary: Plot to establish a restrictive decree against Daniel; only the decree word is shared.

2-chronicles-30:5:3.summary: Royal decree supporting temple sacrifices; general royal-decree-for-worship theme.

2-chronicles-30:5:4.summary: Holding fast to traditions; no specific link to the Passover proclamation.
2-chronicles-30:5:4.why: Only loose idea of following what was written.

2-chronicles-30:5:5.summary: A proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to act “as Moses… directed”; parallel proclamation according to the law.

2-chronicles-30:5:6.summary: Letters sent by couriers to every territory; parallel royal letters, opposite purpose.

2-chronicles-30:5:7.summary: Feasts “you shall proclaim as holy convocations”; legal basis for proclaiming the feast.

2-chronicles-30:5:8.summary: Do not add to or take away from God’s word; no specific link to Passover proclamation.

2-chronicles-30:5:9.summary: Nebuchadnezzar sends letters to all nations; royal-letter parallel only.

2-chronicles-30:5:10.summary: Feasts to “proclaim at their proper times”; contrasts with a delayed Passover.

2-chronicles-30:5:11.summary: Letters written by royal command sent by carriers; royal-letter parallel.

2-chronicles-30:5:12.summary: Josiah’s Passover with “all Judah and Israel”, unparalleled since Samuel; parallel neglected-then-restored Passover.

2-chronicles-30:5:13.summary: Mordecai writes to Jews far and near to establish festival days; parallel written festal summons.

2-chronicles-30:6:0.summary: Runner meets runner carrying news; shares the courier image only.

2-chronicles-30:6:1.summary: Phul king of the Assyrians invades Israel; background to survivors of Assyria.

2-chronicles-30:6:2.summary: Horsemen hurry to carry the king’s decree; courier parallel.

2-chronicles-30:6:3.summary: “If Israel returns… he will return to Me”; same call for Israel to return.

2-chronicles-30:6:5.summary: Phaloch and Thaglathphalnasar, kings of “Assour”, deported northern tribes; the survivors Hezekiah addresses.

2-chronicles-30:6:6.summary: “Let him return to the Lord, and he will receive mercy”; parallel promise attached to returning.

2-chronicles-30:6:7.summary: Life “swifter than a runner”; only the word runner shared.

2-chronicles-30:6:8.summary: Thaglath-phellasar king of Assour struck Ahaz; background to Assyrian pressure.

2-chronicles-30:6:9.summary: “Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you”; parallels “return… and He will bring back.”

2-chronicles-30:6:10.summary: God calls the house of Israel to turn back and live; general call to repentance.

2-chronicles-30:6:11.summary: “A tenth remains”; remnant theme matching the survivors.

2-chronicles-30:6:12.summary: “Turn to the Lord your God… He is merciful”; parallel call to return with hope of God’s turning.

2-chronicles-30:6:13.summary: The Lord “left us seed”; remnant/survivor theme.

2-chronicles-30:6:14.summary: “Turn us back unto Thee, O Lord”; prayer of return.

2-chronicles-30:6:15.summary: “Return, Israel, to the Lord your God”; close verbal parallel to the call to the sons of Israel.
2-chronicles-30:6:15.why: Prophetic call to Israel to return.

2-chronicles-30:7:0.summary: God gave them over to devastation “as you see with your own eyes”; same phrase and judgment idea.
2-chronicles-30:7:0.why: Same Hezekian rhetoric of visible judgment.

2-chronicles-30:7:1.summary: Fathers in the wilderness rejected God’s ordinances and incurred wrath; general warning from the fathers.

2-chronicles-30:7:2.summary: “Do not become like your fathers” who did not listen; nearly identical warning.

2-chronicles-30:8:1.summary: Hezekiah’s earlier covenant aims at the same result: the Lord will “turn His furious wrath away from us.”
2-chronicles-30:8:1.why: Shows the Passover appeal continues Hezekiah’s covenant purpose.

2-chronicles-30:8:3.summary: Both speak of serving or being enslaved to God with sanctification, but Romans is about freedom from sin, not temple worship.
2-chronicles-30:8:3.why: Loose New Testament echo of service and sanctification.

2-chronicles-30:8:4.summary: The Psalm describes God’s wrath sent on Egypt; only the general idea of divine wrath overlaps.
2-chronicles-30:8:4.why: Illustrates the wrath Hezekiah hopes to avert.

2-chronicles-30:8:5.summary: Envoys from Egypt and Ethiopia have no connection to the call not to harden necks or serve the Lord.

2-chronicles-30:8:6.summary: Oded likewise warns that “the Lord’s furious wrath is upon you” and urges a return.
2-chronicles-30:8:6.why: Same Chronicler warning formula in a north-south setting.

2-chronicles-30:8:7.summary: Deuteronomy’s command to “serve Him,” the Lord your God, underlies Hezekiah’s “Serve the Lord your God.”
2-chronicles-30:8:7.why: Grounds the appeal in the Mosaic command.

2-chronicles-30:8:8.summary: Both mention entering God’s “sanctuary,” but the Psalmist enters to understand the wicked’s end.

2-chronicles-30:8:9.summary: Serving God in His temple appears in both, but Revelation describes the heavenly worshippers.

2-chronicles-30:8:10.summary: Zedekiah “hardened his neck” and would not return to the Lord, exactly what Hezekiah warns against.
2-chronicles-30:8:10.why: Shows the later outcome of the stiff neck.

2-chronicles-30:8:11.summary: A disobedient, contrary people loosely matches the stiff-necked hearers, without shared wording.

2-chronicles-30:8:12.summary: Following and serving Jesus shares only the common word “serves.”

2-chronicles-30:8:13.summary: The submission of rulers to Solomon relies on a Hebrew “give the hand” idiom absent from the Greek-based source, which says “Give glory.”
2-chronicles-30:8:13.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

2-chronicles-30:8:14.summary: Giving a hand in pledge to divorce wives depends on a Hebrew idiom not present in the source’s “Give glory.”

2-chronicles-30:8:15.summary: Presenting oneself to God for obedience loosely parallels yielding in service; shown text only, and the source says “Give glory.”
2-chronicles-30:8:15.why: Loose theme of surrender to God.

2-chronicles-30:8:16.summary: Processions in the holy place share only the setting of the sanctuary.

2-chronicles-30:8:17.summary: Jesus quotes “the Lord your God … serve”; the shared phrase is a common formula.
2-chronicles-30:8:17.why: Echo of the basic command to serve God alone.

2-chronicles-30:8:18.summary: Seeing God’s glory in the holy place loosely matches giving glory and entering the sanctuary.

2-chronicles-30:8:19.summary: Joshua’s call to choose to “serve the Lord” is a similar covenant appeal.
2-chronicles-30:8:19.why: Similar call to decide for the Lord.

2-chronicles-30:8:20.summary: Serving the Lord Christ from the heart shares only the general idea of service.

2-chronicles-30:8:21.summary: Under Josiah the Lord did not turn from His “burning wrath,” reversing the hope Hezekiah offers.
2-chronicles-30:8:21.why: Shows the threatened wrath later fell.

2-chronicles-30:8:22.summary: Keeping the commandments of “the Lord your God” is general covenant obedience.

2-chronicles-30:8:23.summary: Zion chosen as God’s dwelling “for age upon age” loosely matches the sanctuary sanctified “for ever.”

2-chronicles-30:8:24.summary: The same phrase “the Lord’s furious wrath is upon Israel” appears in the Ahaz-era episode.
2-chronicles-30:8:24.why: Shows the wrath Hezekiah addresses was already declared.

2-chronicles-30:9:0.summary: Both promise that whoever will “return to the Lord” will receive mercy.

2-chronicles-30:9:1.summary: God not retaining anger because He desires mercy loosely matches the merciful God who will not turn away.

2-chronicles-30:9:2.summary: The Lord “abundant in mercy” is a general statement of His mercy.

2-chronicles-30:9:4.summary: Both speak of compassion “before all who had taken them captive.”
2-chronicles-30:9:4.why: Nearly identical phrasing about captors’ compassion.

2-chronicles-30:9:5.summary: The source’s “merciful and compassionate” echoes the Exodus self-revelation “compassionate and merciful.”
2-chronicles-30:9:5.why: Roots Hezekiah’s confidence in the Sinai name of God.

2-chronicles-30:9:6.summary: Nehemiah links stiff necks with “a merciful and compassionate God” who did not abandon them.
2-chronicles-30:9:6.why: Same pairing of stubbornness and mercy.

2-chronicles-30:9:7.summary: Solomon prays that the Lord would grant compassion “before those who took them captive.”
2-chronicles-30:9:7.why: Shows Hezekiah appealing to Solomon’s temple prayer.

2-chronicles-30:9:8.summary: Confession in the enemies’ land leads God to remember the covenant and “the land.”
2-chronicles-30:9:8.why: Covenant basis for restoration after exile.

2-chronicles-30:9:9.summary: Not hiding impiety and accepting reproof is a general repentance theme.

2-chronicles-30:9:10.summary: Azariah’s conditional promise, “If you seek Him, He shall be found,” parallels “if we return to Him.”

2-chronicles-30:9:11.summary: God rebuilding and planting Israel and Judah loosely matches bringing them back to the land.

2-chronicles-30:9:12.summary: “The Lord is merciful and compassionate” is the same formula.

2-chronicles-30:9:13.summary: God, “merciful and compassionate,” did not abandon His people.
2-chronicles-30:9:13.why: Same formula and promise of not forsaking.

2-chronicles-30:9:14.summary: “Compassionate and merciful is the Lord” repeats the formula.

2-chronicles-30:9:15.summary: Seeking God and finding Him parallels returning to Him; the shown Septuagint text lacks any return from captivity.
2-chronicles-30:9:15.why: General promise to those who seek.

2-chronicles-30:9:16.summary: Jonah cites God as “merciful and compassionate,” the same formula.

2-chronicles-30:9:17.summary: The Psalm calls the Lord “compassionate and merciful.”

2-chronicles-30:9:18.summary: The Greek text speaks of scattering and a day of destruction, not turning the face, so the assumed link is absent.

2-chronicles-30:9:19.summary: God promises to hear if His people seek His face and turn, matching Hezekiah’s promise.
2-chronicles-30:9:19.why: Hezekiah relies on the promise given at the temple dedication.

2-chronicles-30:9:20.summary: The call to “turn back” from impieties shares the repentance theme generally.

2-chronicles-30:10:1.summary: The same “runners” carrying the king’s letters are described setting out.
2-chronicles-30:10:1.why: Immediate context of the mocked messengers.

2-chronicles-30:10:2.summary: Opponents “laughed at us” as Nehemiah worked, a general mockery theme.
2-chronicles-30:10:2.why: Similar ridicule of a restoration effort.

2-chronicles-30:10:3.summary: Job’s life “swifter than a runner” shares only the word runner.

2-chronicles-30:10:4.summary: Jesus mocked by His captors shares only the theme of mockery.
2-chronicles-30:10:4.why: General theme of rejecting God’s messenger.

2-chronicles-30:10:5.summary: Lot’s warning seemed “like someone joking,” as the runners’ warning was met with laughter.
2-chronicles-30:10:5.why: Same pattern of a warning ridiculed before judgment.

2-chronicles-30:10:6.summary: The Pharisees sneered at Jesus’ teaching, a general mockery theme.
2-chronicles-30:10:6.why: General theme of scorn for God’s word.

2-chronicles-30:10:7.summary: Royal letters sent by letter carriers resemble Hezekiah’s runners.

2-chronicles-30:10:8.summary: They “laughed at Him” at Jairus’s house, a general mockery theme.

2-chronicles-30:10:9.summary: A hurried decree in Susa has no real connection to the runners being mocked.

2-chronicles-30:10:10.summary: Some mocked and others listened, a mixed response like 30:10–11.
2-chronicles-30:10:10.why: Similar divided response to a message.

2-chronicles-30:10:11.summary: Mockery suffered by the faithful is a general theme.

2-chronicles-30:10:12.summary: Letters sent “by couriers” throughout a kingdom resemble Hezekiah’s runners.

2-chronicles-30:10:13.summary: Horsemen hurrying with a royal decree resemble the runners only generally.

2-chronicles-30:10:14.summary: A righteous man made an object of mockery shares only the general theme.

2-chronicles-30:10:15.summary: Rulers sneered at Christ, a general theme of mockery.

2-chronicles-30:11:0.summary: The same northern tribes, Manasse and Zaboulon, appear among those who came and ate the Passover.

2-chronicles-30:11:1.summary: The “sons of Israel present in Jerusalem” are those who came, keeping the feast.

2-chronicles-30:11:2.summary: “Those present from Israel” rejoice at the same Passover.

2-chronicles-30:11:3.summary: Humbling oneself and being exalted is general; the source’s Greek says “felt shame.”

2-chronicles-30:11:4.summary: The self-humbling tax collector loosely parallels those who “felt shame.”

2-chronicles-30:11:5.summary: “Humble yourselves before the Lord” is a general theme; the source says “felt shame.”

2-chronicles-30:11:6.summary: Pharaoh’s refusal “to reverence” God lacks the Hebrew “humble” the label assumes.
2-chronicles-30:11:6.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

2-chronicles-30:11:7.summary: The repentant heart that “will feel shame” uses the same verb for turning back to God.
2-chronicles-30:11:7.why: Covenant pattern of shame leading to return.

2-chronicles-30:11:8.summary: Rehoboam “felt shame” and the Lord’s wrath turned away.
2-chronicles-30:11:8.why: Same Chronicler verb with the same result.

2-chronicles-30:11:9.summary: Some joined Paul amid mockery, a mixed response like 30:10–11.

2-chronicles-30:11:10.summary: Israel’s rulers and king “felt shame,” and God spared them.

2-chronicles-30:11:11.summary: Faithful people from Israel’s tribes came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord.
2-chronicles-30:11:11.why: Earlier precedent of northerners coming to Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-30:11:13.summary: Manasseh “humbled himself greatly” is the same repentance theme in different wording.

2-chronicles-30:11:14.summary: The shown text lists Manasseh’s prayer and sins but nothing about shame or coming to Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-30:11:15.summary: “Humble yourselves” is a general humility exhortation.

2-chronicles-30:11:16.summary: Amon “did not humble himself,” a loose contrast to those who felt shame.

2-chronicles-30:11:17.summary: Josiah’s “heart felt shame” uses the same verb of repentant humility.

2-chronicles-30:12:0.summary: God promises, “I will give them … another heart,” as the Lord’s hand gave Judah one heart.

2-chronicles-30:12:1.summary: God working in believers to will and work loosely matches His hand moving Judah.

2-chronicles-30:12:2.summary: “I will give them a heart to know Me” shares the idea of God giving a heart.
2-chronicles-30:12:2.why: General promise of a God-given heart.

2-chronicles-30:12:3.summary: The Greek Psalm speaks of rule and begetting, with no willing people or heart.

2-chronicles-30:12:4.summary: God choosing and calling believers is general divine initiative.

2-chronicles-30:12:5.summary: “I will give you a new heart” loosely parallels God giving one heart.
2-chronicles-30:12:5.why: General promise of a new heart.

2-chronicles-30:12:7.summary: Keeping ordinances as the Lord commanded shares only general obedience.

2-chronicles-30:12:8.summary: Again a royal ordinance comes “by the Lord’s command through the prophets,” in Hezekiah’s reform.
2-chronicles-30:12:8.why: Same pairing of king’s order and the Lord’s word.

2-chronicles-30:12:9.summary: Instructions given through the Lord Jesus share only the idea of commands.

2-chronicles-30:12:10.summary: David asks God to direct the people’s hearts toward Him.

2-chronicles-30:12:11.summary: Keeping the word the Lord commands is general obedience.

2-chronicles-30:12:12.summary: Obeying God over rulers contrasts loosely with rulers whose order matched the Lord’s word.
2-chronicles-30:12:12.why: Loose contrast about human and divine authority.

2-chronicles-30:12:13.summary: God putting a purpose in the king’s heart loosely matches His hand moving Judah.

2-chronicles-30:13:0.summary: The decision to keep the Passover “in the second month” is the same event.

2-chronicles-30:13:1.summary: Pilgrims going to Zion where God appears loosely matches the gathering in Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-30:14:1.summary: Uncleanness from the temple was likewise cast “into the Kedron torrent.”
2-chronicles-30:14:1.why: Same disposal site in the same reform.

2-chronicles-30:14:2.summary: Asa burned the idol “in the Kedron torrent.”
2-chronicles-30:14:2.why: Earlier reform using the same site.

2-chronicles-30:14:3.summary: David crossed “the Kidron torrent,” sharing only the place.

2-chronicles-30:14:4.summary: Josiah pulled down altars and threw their dust “into the Kidron torrent.”
2-chronicles-30:14:4.why: Later reform with the same action and place.

2-chronicles-30:14:5.summary: Josiah “pulled down” altars and idols in a similar purge.

2-chronicles-30:14:6.summary: Josiah “pulled down … the altars of the Baals,” the same reform act.

2-chronicles-30:14:7.summary: People casting away their idols is a general prophetic image.

2-chronicles-30:14:8.summary: The Assyrian cites Hezekiah’s removal of “high places and altars.”

2-chronicles-30:14:9.summary: Jesus crosses the Kidron, sharing only the place.

2-chronicles-30:15:0.summary: Priests and Levites purified themselves during Hezekiah’s earlier temple service.
2-chronicles-30:15:0.why: Background on the priests’ slowness to purify.

2-chronicles-30:15:1.summary: Purifying the people before meeting God is a general purity theme.

2-chronicles-30:15:2.summary: Priests “sanctified” at the temple dedication is a general purity parallel.

2-chronicles-30:15:3.summary: The Greek speaks of ceasing from sins and receiving punishment, not shame, so the link is absent.

2-chronicles-30:15:4.summary: Priests who “purified the holy place” share a general purity theme.

2-chronicles-30:15:5.summary: Being ashamed before God’s mercy is only loosely related to the priests’ shame.

2-chronicles-30:15:6.summary: Priests must consecrate themselves before approaching God, a general requirement.

2-chronicles-30:15:7.summary: The Levites “purified themselves” at Hezekiah’s command in the same reform.

2-chronicles-30:15:8.summary: The same Passover’s offerings are described, with the priests’ holy things abundant.

2-chronicles-30:16:0.summary: At Josiah’s Passover the singers were “at their station according to the commands,” a parallel arrangement.

2-chronicles-30:16:1.summary: “Moses, the man of God” is the same title, but the context is unrelated.

2-chronicles-30:16:2.summary: Standing “according to the ordinance” is a loose verbal overlap in an unrelated scene.

2-chronicles-30:16:3.summary: Passover and the sprinkling of blood loosely match the priests handling the blood.

2-chronicles-30:17:0.summary: The Levites helped earlier because the priests were few and not yet purified.
2-chronicles-30:17:0.why: Same Levitical role in Hezekiah’s reform.

2-chronicles-30:17:2.summary: The Passover law has the congregation slaughter on the fourteenth, explaining why Levites stood in for the unclean.
2-chronicles-30:17:2.why: Shows the normal rule being adapted.

2-chronicles-30:18:0.summary: Prayer for sinners leading to healing loosely anticipates Hezekiah’s intercession.

2-chronicles-30:18:1.summary: Examining oneself before eating the bread is a loose parallel to eating the Passover unprepared.

2-chronicles-30:18:3.summary: “Lord, be propitious!” echoes Hezekiah’s plea that the Lord “be propitious.”

2-chronicles-30:18:4.summary: Solomon asks God to “hear and be propitious” to the people.
2-chronicles-30:18:4.why: Hezekiah’s plea draws on the temple prayer.

2-chronicles-30:18:5.summary: The law says one “not purified” defiles the Lord’s holy things.
2-chronicles-30:18:5.why: Shows the risk the unpurified faced.

2-chronicles-30:18:6.summary: The same northern tribes came to Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-30:18:7.summary: Those present from Israel rejoice at the same Passover.

2-chronicles-30:18:8.summary: Abraham as intercessor who will “pray for you” is a general intercession parallel.

2-chronicles-30:18:9.summary: The Passover law on eligibility relates generally to eating “contrary to the writing”; shown text concerns foreigners.

2-chronicles-30:18:10.summary: “The Lord is kind” to sinners echoes “the good Lord” only loosely.

2-chronicles-30:18:11.summary: Abraham’s prayer leading to healing loosely parallels Hezekiah’s prayer.

2-chronicles-30:18:12.summary: Job intercedes and sin is released, a general intercession parallel.

2-chronicles-30:18:13.summary: “Thou art good, Lord” shares only the attribute of goodness.

2-chronicles-30:18:14.summary: Asking for a brother who sins is a general intercession teaching.

2-chronicles-30:18:15.summary: The Lord “kind and forbearing” loosely matches “the good Lord.”

2-chronicles-30:18:16.summary: Moses asks God to forgive the people’s sin and God pardons them.

2-chronicles-30:18:17.summary: Moses asks pardon for a stiff-necked people, a general intercession parallel.

2-chronicles-30:18:18.summary: God’s mercy reaching heaven is only a general mercy statement.
