2-chronicles-33:1:7.summary: Josiah’s accession uses the same age-and-length formula as Manasseh’s, with contrasting conduct.

2-chronicles-33:1:1.summary: The genealogy lists “Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,” naming the same king.

2-chronicles-33:1:2.summary: God setting young men as rulers loosely relates to Manasseh beginning to reign at twelve.

2-chronicles-33:1:3.summary: Oppressors lording over the people shares no specific element with Manasseh’s accession age and reign.
2-chronicles-33:1:3.why: No real connection in this wording.

2-chronicles-33:1:4.summary: Woe to a city whose king is young loosely relates to Manasseh reigning at twelve.

2-chronicles-33:1:5.summary: Matthew’s genealogy names “Hezekiah begot Manasseh,” the same king.

2-chronicles-33:1:6.summary: The preceding verse states “his son Manasseh reigned in his place,” introducing the source.

2-chronicles-33:2:0.summary: Ahaz acted “according to the abominations of the nations the Lord had destroyed before the sons of Israel,” the identical phrase.

2-chronicles-33:2:1.summary: The law forbids learning “the abominations of those nations,” which Manasseh followed.

2-chronicles-33:2:2.summary: Judah’s leaders multiplied the “nations’ abominations,” continuing Manasseh’s pattern.
2-chronicles-33:2:2.why: Shows the sin’s persistence to exile.

2-chronicles-33:2:3.summary: The shown text “you will recognize that I am the Lord” lacks the source’s mention of the nations’ ways.
2-chronicles-33:2:3.why: No link in the shown wording.

2-chronicles-33:2:4.summary: Israel must not walk in the laws of the nations God drove out, which Manasseh did.

2-chronicles-33:2:5.summary: The dispossessed nations’ omens and divinations relate to Manasseh’s practices, though the source verse is general.

2-chronicles-33:2:6.summary: Israel acted “like the nations whom the Lord deported before them,” matching the source’s formula.

2-chronicles-33:2:7.summary: The nations’ “abominations” including child burning are what Manasseh followed.

2-chronicles-33:2:8.summary: Ezra confesses mixing with peoples of the lands, generally like following nations’ abominations.
2-chronicles-33:2:8.why: Later confession of the same sin.

2-chronicles-33:2:10.summary: Israel must avoid the “abominations” by which the nations driven out were defiled, which Manasseh followed.

2-chronicles-33:2:11.summary: Israel followed the surrounding nations against God’s command, the same sin pattern as Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:2:12.summary: Kings says Manasseh led them to do evil beyond the nations the Lord obliterated, the parallel account.

2-chronicles-33:2:13.summary: Jeremiah names Manasseh son of Hezekiah and his deeds in Jerusalem as cause of judgment.
2-chronicles-33:2:13.why: Shows the consequences of his evil.

2-chronicles-33:2:14.summary: Israel mixed with the nations, learned their works and sacrificed sons, as Manasseh did.

2-chronicles-33:3:0.summary: The law forbids planting a “sacred grove,” which Manasseh made.

2-chronicles-33:3:1.summary: The law forbids bowing to “the array of heaven,” which Manasseh worshiped.

2-chronicles-33:3:2.summary: Under Hezekiah Israel shattered pillars, cut down groves and demolished high places—what Manasseh rebuilt.

2-chronicles-33:3:3.summary: Hezekiah’s people demolished altars in Jerusalem, a general contrast to Manasseh’s rebuilding.

2-chronicles-33:3:4.summary: “One sinner will destroy much good” loosely fits Manasseh undoing Hezekiah’s reforms.

2-chronicles-33:3:5.summary: Hezekiah removed the high places, pillars and groves, the very things Manasseh rebuilt.

2-chronicles-33:3:6.summary: Josiah ended incense to Baal and “all heaven’s host” and removed the grove, undoing Manasseh-type worship.
2-chronicles-33:3:6.why: Later reform against the same cults.

2-chronicles-33:3:7.summary: Incense to “all the host of the heavens” in Judah’s houses matches Manasseh’s worship of heaven’s army.

2-chronicles-33:3:8.summary: Zephaniah condemns “those worshiping the army of heaven,” the cult Manasseh served.
2-chronicles-33:3:8.why: Prophetic condemnation of the same cult.

2-chronicles-33:3:9.summary: An heir may be foolish and undo his predecessor’s labor, loosely fitting Manasseh after Hezekiah.

2-chronicles-33:3:10.summary: Hezekiah removed the high places and altars, the ones Manasseh rebuilt.

2-chronicles-33:3:11.summary: Josiah removed horses and chariots given to the sun, a related astral cult but not Manasseh’s specific acts.

2-chronicles-33:3:12.summary: Judgment on those who served and bowed down to “all heaven’s host,” as Manasseh did.

2-chronicles-33:3:13.summary: Ahaz made images and burned incense at high places, the same apostasy Manasseh revived.

2-chronicles-33:3:14.summary: Israel served the Baalim and bowed to other gods, generally like Manasseh’s pillars for the Baals.

2-chronicles-33:3:15.summary: Moses warns against bowing to and serving the sun, moon and stars, which Manasseh did.

2-chronicles-33:3:17.summary: Judah built high places, standing stones and groves, the same cult items Manasseh restored.
2-chronicles-33:3:17.why: Earlier instance of the same idolatry.

2-chronicles-33:3:18.summary: God handed Israel over to worship “the host of heaven,” loosely echoing Manasseh’s worship.

2-chronicles-33:4:0.summary: God chose this house “for My name to be there for ever,” the promise the source cites.

2-chronicles-33:4:1.summary: The place God chooses for His name generally underlies the source’s promise about Jerusalem.
2-chronicles-33:4:1.why: Deuteronomic background of the chosen place.

2-chronicles-33:4:2.summary: “I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there” echoes the cited promise.

2-chronicles-33:4:3.summary: Solomon recalls God saying “My name shall be there,” matching the cited word.

2-chronicles-33:4:4.summary: Josiah pulled down Baal altars and high places, a general reversal of Manasseh’s altars.

2-chronicles-33:4:5.summary: Manasseh later removed the altars he had built in the Lord’s house.

2-chronicles-33:4:7.summary: Abominations set in “the house over which My name has been called” matches altars in the house of God’s name.

2-chronicles-33:4:8.summary: God consecrated the house “to put My name there for ever,” the promise cited.

2-chronicles-33:4:9.summary: Sennacherib speaking against Jerusalem’s God shares no specific link with Manasseh’s altars in the temple.

2-chronicles-33:5:0.summary: Solomon made the priests’ court and great court, the two temple courtyards where Manasseh built altars.

2-chronicles-33:5:1.summary: Ezekiel sees abominations and idolatry inside the temple courtyard, like Manasseh’s altars in the courtyards.

2-chronicles-33:5:2.summary: They set pollutions in the house called by God’s name and built Baal altars, like Manasseh’s temple altars.

2-chronicles-33:6:17.summary: Israel led children through fire, practiced divination and omens, provoking the Lord, the same list as Manasseh’s.

2-chronicles-33:6:0.summary: The LXX ban on giving seed “to serve a ruler” relates to child sacrifice only indirectly in this wording.

2-chronicles-33:6:1.summary: The law forbids following “spirit mediums” and “enchanters,” which Manasseh appointed.

2-chronicles-33:6:3.summary: Ahaz sacrificed in Gaibenenom and made his children pass through fire, exactly like Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:6:4.summary: God sets His face against one following “spirit mediums or enchanters,” which Manasseh appointed.

2-chronicles-33:6:5.summary: The law forbids divining by omens and observing birds, matching Manasseh’s omens and augury.

2-chronicles-33:6:6.summary: Isaiah rebukes seeking belly-speakers and the dead, the mediumship Manasseh promoted.

2-chronicles-33:6:7.summary: Saul died for inquiring “through the spirit medium,” the practice Manasseh appointed.

2-chronicles-33:6:8.summary: Burning children in fire in the ravine of the son of Hinnom matches Manasseh in Gai-banai-ennom.

2-chronicles-33:6:9.summary: Babylon’s “sorcery” and “enchanters” share vocabulary with Manasseh’s practices but concern another nation.

2-chronicles-33:6:10.summary: Death penalty for giving seed “unto a ruler” relates to child offering only indirectly in this LXX wording.

2-chronicles-33:6:12.summary: Egypt inquiring of those speaking from the earth and belly-speakers resembles mediumship, in a foreign context.

2-chronicles-33:6:13.summary: Josiah removed charmers and knowing ones, the kind of practitioners Manasseh had appointed.

2-chronicles-33:6:14.summary: Slaughtering children for idols while defiling God’s house matches Manasseh’s sins.

2-chronicles-33:6:15.summary: The nations burned sons and daughters with fire, the abomination Manasseh practiced.

2-chronicles-33:6:16.summary: “Divination is sin” relates generally to Manasseh’s omens and augury.

2-chronicles-33:6:18.summary: “Sorcery” appears in Paul’s vice list, a general link to Manasseh’s sorcery.

2-chronicles-33:6:19.summary: They made their children “pass through fire,” the same act Manasseh did.

2-chronicles-33:6:20.summary: A “spirit-medium or an enchanter” is to be put to death; Manasseh appointed such.

2-chronicles-33:6:21.summary: Josiah defiled Tapheth in the valley of the son of Ennom, where children passed through fire as under Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:7:0.summary: Manasseh built altars in the house of which the Lord said “My name shall be in Jerusalem for ever,” the same promise invoked.

2-chronicles-33:7:1.summary: God chose and sanctified this house “for My name to be there for ever,” the promise the source quotes.

2-chronicles-33:7:2.summary: The Lord chose Zion as His dwelling “for age upon age,” loosely echoing God’s chosen house and city.

2-chronicles-33:7:3.summary: “Jerusalem, the city I have chosen” echoes the source’s Jerusalem chosen by God.

2-chronicles-33:7:4.summary: Manasseh later removed “the carved object from the Lord’s house,” the same image he set there.

2-chronicles-33:7:5.summary: “I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there” matches the promise the source cites.

2-chronicles-33:7:6.summary: Josiah removed the grove from the Lord’s house, related to idols placed in the temple but not this act.

2-chronicles-33:7:7.summary: “Jerusalem, the city I chose from all Israel’s tribes” closely matches the source’s wording.

2-chronicles-33:7:8.summary: God chose Judah’s tribe and Mount Zion, generally like choosing Jerusalem out of Israel’s tribes.

2-chronicles-33:7:10.summary: The place of which God said “My name shall be there” matches the promise about this house.

2-chronicles-33:7:11.summary: “The city Thou didst choose and the house I built for Thy name” shares wording but in a prayer context.

2-chronicles-33:7:12.summary: “The city Thou didst choose, and the house I have built for Thy name” shares the chosen-city phrasing only.

2-chronicles-33:8:0.summary: God promises to plant Israel in its place undisturbed, generally like not shaking Israel from the land.

2-chronicles-33:8:1.summary: Only an introductory formula is shown, sharing nothing specific with the land promise.

2-chronicles-33:8:2.summary: The curse on not doing “all the things written in the book of the law” touches the conditional obedience in the source.

2-chronicles-33:8:3.summary: Obeying God’s ordinances and judgments brings life in the land; turning away brings loss of it, the same condition.

2-chronicles-33:8:4.summary: Moses calls Israel to do “the ordinances and the judgments,” a general echo of the source’s condition.

2-chronicles-33:8:5.summary: The statutes spoken “by the hand of Moses” loosely echo the law given through Moses in the source.

2-chronicles-33:8:6.summary: God’s promise to Solomon conditions remaining in the land on keeping His ordinances and judgments, as here.

2-chronicles-33:8:7.summary: Keeping His ordinances and commandments to prolong days on the land matches the source’s condition.

2-chronicles-33:8:8.summary: Aaron doing what the Lord directed Moses shares only incidental wording with the land promise.

2-chronicles-33:8:9.summary: Blessings in the land depend on doing all His commandments, matching the source’s conditional promise.

2-chronicles-33:8:10.summary: Doing all the commandments to inherit the land sworn to the fathers parallels the source’s condition.

2-chronicles-33:8:11.summary: God will plant His people undisturbed in their place, generally like not shaking Israel from the land.

2-chronicles-33:8:12.summary: Listening yields the land’s good things, refusing brings the sword; a general obedience condition.

2-chronicles-33:8:13.summary: Commandments, ordinances and judgments to be done in the land God gives, with long days, match the source.

2-chronicles-33:8:14.summary: Walking in “all the Lord’s commandments and ordinances” echoes the source’s phrase but concerns Zechariah and Elizabeth.

2-chronicles-33:9:0.summary: Manasseh followed the abominations of the nations the Lord destroyed before Israel, the same charge.

2-chronicles-33:9:1.summary: An unjust king makes his subjects lawless, generally fitting Manasseh leading Judah astray.

2-chronicles-33:9:2.summary: Judah’s removal came because of Manasseh’s sins and innocent blood, the consequence of his leading them astray.

2-chronicles-33:9:3.summary: Israel walked in the ordinances of the nations the Lord removed before them, the same formula.

2-chronicles-33:9:5.summary: The Lord’s wrath against Judah due to Manasseh’s provocations follows from his leading Judah astray.

2-chronicles-33:9:7.summary: Nadab caused Israel to sin, a general parallel to Manasseh leading Judah astray.

2-chronicles-33:9:8.summary: Manasseh caused Judah to do evil in the Lord’s eyes, the parallel record in Kings.

2-chronicles-33:9:9.summary: Keeping Omri’s and Ahab’s practices led to ruin, generally like following wicked leadership.

2-chronicles-33:9:10.summary: The nations driven out were defiled by these things, the standard Manasseh exceeded.

2-chronicles-33:9:11.summary: The Lord destroying the Anakim before the Ammonites shares only the dispossession idea, not Manasseh’s sin.

2-chronicles-33:9:12.summary: God destroyed the Amorites before Israel, background to the nations removed but not to Manasseh’s sin.

2-chronicles-33:9:13.summary: Jerusalem surpasses Samaria and Sodom in lawlessness, like Manasseh doing evil beyond the nations.

2-chronicles-33:10:0.summary: The Lord sent prophets but the people mocked them, the same pattern of ignored warning.

2-chronicles-33:10:1.summary: God testified to them through prophets “but they did not listen,” matching the source.

2-chronicles-33:10:2.summary: Prophets warned the fathers but “they did not listen,” paralleling Manasseh’s people.

2-chronicles-33:10:3.summary: God sent prophets warning against defilement but “they did not listen,” as here.

2-chronicles-33:10:4.summary: God sent prophets repeatedly and “you did not listen,” matching the source’s refusal.

2-chronicles-33:10:5.summary: Stephen indicts Israel for always resisting God and the prophets, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-33:11:0.summary: The Lord would lead the king to a foreign nation, a curse fulfilled when Manasseh was taken to Babylon.

2-chronicles-33:11:1.summary: Jehoiakim was bound with bronze fetters and taken to Babylon, the same fate as Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:11:2.summary: Those fettered for spurning God cried out and He broke their bonds, mirroring Manasseh’s chains and restoration.

2-chronicles-33:11:3.summary: The fragment about Assyria’s king being sole ruler shares no specific link with Manasseh’s capture.

2-chronicles-33:11:4.summary: Pharaoh removed Jehoahaz from reigning, a loose parallel of a Judean king taken by a foreign power.

2-chronicles-33:11:5.summary: Rapsakes’ taunt about facing a governor has no specific link to Manasseh’s capture.

2-chronicles-33:11:6.summary: “He made my bronze heavy” evokes God-imposed fetters, loosely like Manasseh bound in fetters.

2-chronicles-33:11:7.summary: Israelites hiding in caves before the Philistines shares nothing specific with Manasseh’s capture.

2-chronicles-33:11:8.summary: Zedekiah was seized and brought to Babylon’s king, a similar royal capture though different event.

2-chronicles-33:11:9.summary: God summons distant nations against His people, generally like the Lord bringing Assyria’s commanders.

2-chronicles-33:11:10.summary: Those fettered in handcuffs are shown their transgressions to turn back, matching Manasseh’s chastening.

2-chronicles-33:11:11.summary: The Lord summons Assyria as His instrument against Judah, generally like the source.

2-chronicles-33:11:12.summary: Nehemiah recalls hardship on kings “from the days of the kings of Assour,” a general background.

2-chronicles-33:11:13.summary: Foreign kings rule over Israel because of their sins, generally like Manasseh’s capture.

2-chronicles-33:12:0.summary: Pharaoh refused to humble himself before God, contrasting with Manasseh humbling himself.
2-chronicles-33:12:0.why: Contrast of proud and humbled kings.

2-chronicles-33:12:1.summary: “Call on Me in the day of affliction; I will rescue you” fits Manasseh seeking God when afflicted.

2-chronicles-33:12:2.summary: Hezekiah humbled himself and wrath was averted, paralleling Manasseh humbling himself greatly.

2-chronicles-33:12:3.summary: “The one who humbles himself will be exalted” fits Manasseh’s humbling and restoration in principle.

2-chronicles-33:12:4.summary: Saul the persecutor is found praying, a loose parallel to a sinner turning to prayer.

2-chronicles-33:12:6.summary: “They will seek My face, and in their affliction” rise early toward God, matching Manasseh’s response.

2-chronicles-33:12:7.summary: “Humble yourselves before the Lord” states the principle Manasseh enacted.

2-chronicles-33:12:8.summary: God gives grace to the humble, a general principle seen in Manasseh’s case.

2-chronicles-33:12:9.summary: Exiles confessing sins in enemy lands and God remembering His covenant matches Manasseh’s repentance in Babylon.
2-chronicles-33:12:9.why: Covenant pattern of repentance in exile.

2-chronicles-33:12:10.summary: Amon did not humble himself “as his father Manasseh had humbled himself,” recalling this event.

2-chronicles-33:12:11.summary: Ephraim repents after discipline and captivity and finds mercy, a general parallel to Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:12:12.summary: The Lord’s voice calling to the city shares no specific element with Manasseh’s humbling.

2-chronicles-33:12:13.summary: Ahaz was delivered into Syria’s hand, a similar affliction but without repentance.

2-chronicles-33:12:14.summary: Ahaz “when he was afflicted” departed further from the Lord, the opposite of Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:12:15.summary: The prodigal comes to himself in distress and returns to his father, a loose parallel.

2-chronicles-33:12:16.summary: Manasseh’s prayer and God listening to him are recorded, the same repentance.

2-chronicles-33:13:0.summary: They cried to God and “He listened to them,” a general parallel to God listening to Manasseh.
2-chronicles-33:13:0.why: God hears those who cry out.

2-chronicles-33:13:1.summary: Ezra’s group sought God and He heard them, a general parallel.

2-chronicles-33:13:2.summary: Nebuchadnezzar to be led away into custody loosely relates to a humbled king later restored.

2-chronicles-33:13:3.summary: Ask and seek and it will be given, a general principle of answered prayer.

2-chronicles-33:13:4.summary: Seeking God’s kingdom first shares only general seeking, not Manasseh’s answered prayer.

2-chronicles-33:13:5.summary: “Pray to Me, and I will listen to you,” addressed to exiles, matches God listening to Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:13:6.summary: God gives a heart to know “that I am the Lord,” echoing Manasseh knowing the Lord is God.

2-chronicles-33:13:7.summary: Nebuchadnezzar entreated God after humbling and his kingship was restored, closely like Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:13:8.summary: God directing a king’s heart shares no specific element with Manasseh’s prayer and restoration.

2-chronicles-33:13:9.summary: The Lord is abundant in mercy to all who call on Him, the mercy Manasseh received.

2-chronicles-33:13:10.summary: The ungodly who returns to the Lord receives mercy and abundant forgiveness, as Manasseh did.

2-chronicles-33:13:11.summary: “That you might know that He is the Lord your God” echoes Manasseh knowing the Lord is God.

2-chronicles-33:13:12.summary: Turning back and humbling oneself before the Lord fits Manasseh’s repentance in principle.

2-chronicles-33:13:13.summary: Jesus offering living water to the Samaritan woman shares nothing specific with Manasseh’s prayer.

2-chronicles-33:13:14.summary: “The Lord is known as He executes judgments” loosely relates to Manasseh knowing God through events.

2-chronicles-33:13:15.summary: Knowing “the only true God” loosely echoes Manasseh knowing the Lord Himself is God.

2-chronicles-33:13:16.summary: The repentant thief receives mercy at the end, loosely like a great sinner heard.

2-chronicles-33:13:17.summary: This LXX proverb on righteous deeds over sacrifices does not carry the link to Manasseh’s answered prayer.

2-chronicles-33:13:18.summary: “Know that I am God” echoes Manasseh knowing the Lord is God.

2-chronicles-33:13:19.summary: All knowing the Lord in the new covenant shares only the verb “know,” not Manasseh’s story.

2-chronicles-33:13:20.summary: God chastens a person to turn him from injustice and spares his soul, a general pattern like Manasseh’s.

2-chronicles-33:13:21.summary: “When you pray to Him, He will hear you” matches Manasseh praying and God listening.

2-chronicles-33:13:22.summary: God moving Artaxerxes to glorify the temple shares no specific element with Manasseh’s prayer.

2-chronicles-33:13:23.summary: Confession of sin bringing forgiveness after God’s heavy hand loosely parallels Manasseh’s repentance.

2-chronicles-33:14:1.summary: The Fish Gate rebuilt in Nehemiah; Manasseh’s wall reached toward a gate, but this verse names no shared feature.

2-chronicles-33:14:2.summary: Gihon, named in Solomon’s anointing, is the landmark Manasseh’s wall ran opposite.

2-chronicles-33:14:3.summary: Zephaniah’s cry from a gate and quarter shares no specific element with Manasseh’s wall in this wording.
2-chronicles-33:14:3.why: No clear link in shown text.

2-chronicles-33:14:4.summary: The Fish Gate and other Jerusalem gates appear, loosely related to the city walls Manasseh built.

2-chronicles-33:14:5.summary: Jehoshaphat stationed men in Judea’s fortified cities, like Manasseh stationing commanders in walled cities.

2-chronicles-33:14:6.summary: Hezekiah built an outer wall and strengthened the City of David, similar wall-building there.

2-chronicles-33:14:7.summary: The Ophal and the wall of the Ophla are the same area Manasseh’s wall reached.

2-chronicles-33:14:8.summary: Hezekiah’s Gihon works and the southwest of the City of David name the same location as Manasseh’s wall.

2-chronicles-33:14:9.summary: Solomon was anointed at Gihon, sharing only the place name.

2-chronicles-33:14:10.summary: Rehoboam fortified cities and placed leaders in them, as Manasseh stationed commanders in walled cities.

2-chronicles-33:15:1.summary: Returning to God and no longer calling handmade works “Our gods” fits Manasseh removing idols.

2-chronicles-33:15:2.summary: Manasseh placed the carved image in the Lord’s house, the same carved object he later removed.

2-chronicles-33:15:3.summary: People will cast away their handmade idols, generally like Manasseh removing his idols.

2-chronicles-33:15:4.summary: The lawless person who turns will live, a principle illustrated by Manasseh’s reforms.

2-chronicles-33:15:5.summary: “Fruit worthy of repentance” loosely describes Manasseh removing idols after repenting.
2-chronicles-33:15:5.note: Quoted wording here is paraphrased or comes from Hebrew-based translations, not the Saints text; compare the Saints readings.

2-chronicles-33:16:0.summary: Asa “told Judah to seek the Lord,” the same royal command as Manasseh telling Judah to serve the Lord.

2-chronicles-33:16:1.summary: Peter, once turned back, should strengthen his brothers, loosely like Manasseh leading Judah after repenting.

2-chronicles-33:16:2.summary: Abraham commanding his household to keep the Lord’s ways loosely parallels Manasseh instructing Judah.

2-chronicles-33:16:3.summary: The shown verse only has Elijah calling the people near, without the altar repair that follows.

2-chronicles-33:16:4.summary: The law of the sacrifice of “deliverance” brought “for praise” matches Manasseh’s offering of salvation and praise.

2-chronicles-33:16:5.summary: Manasseh had led Judah astray; now he tells Judah to serve the Lord, reversing his earlier influence.
2-chronicles-33:16:5.why: Shows the reversal of his leadership.

2-chronicles-33:16:6.summary: Hezekiah’s priests purified the altar of burnt offering, like Manasseh setting the Lord’s altar right.

2-chronicles-33:16:7.summary: Judah given one heart to obey the king’s ordinance loosely parallels Manasseh commanding Judah to serve the Lord.

2-chronicles-33:16:8.summary: The law of the “sacrifice of deliverance” describes the offering of salvation Manasseh sacrificed.

2-chronicles-33:17:0.summary: Hezekiah removed the high places and centralized worship at one altar, the ideal the people still fell short of.

2-chronicles-33:17:1.summary: Under Asa the high places did not depart, yet his heart was complete, a similar qualified reform.

2-chronicles-33:17:2.summary: The people still sacrificed at the high places, the same lingering practice noted here.

2-chronicles-33:17:3.summary: Jehoshaphat did right, but the shown verse lacks the high-places remark; the link is only to qualified good reigns.

2-chronicles-33:18:0.summary: The next verse completes the source sentence about Manasseh’s prayer recorded in the seers’ accounts.

2-chronicles-33:18:2.summary: Amaziah calling Amos “Seer” shares only the word, not Manasseh’s seers or records.

2-chronicles-33:18:3.summary: People silencing seers loosely relates to the seers who spoke to Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:18:4.summary: Jehoshaphat’s acts written in the accounts of Jehu son of Anani uses the same prophetic-source formula.

2-chronicles-33:18:5.summary: God closing the eyes of seers shares only the seer theme, not Manasseh’s record.

2-chronicles-33:18:6.summary: Hezekiah’s remaining deeds are written in Isaiah’s prophecy and the Book of Kings, the same closing formula.

2-chronicles-33:18:7.summary: The Lord warned through every prophet and seer, generally like the seers who spoke to Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:18:8.summary: Shamed seers and diviners share only vocabulary with the source.

2-chronicles-33:18:9.summary: The Lord spoke against Manasseh and his people, the seers’ words the source mentions.

2-chronicles-33:18:11.summary: “The rest of Nadab’s acts… written” uses the same regnal source formula.

2-chronicles-33:18:12.summary: Explains that prophets were formerly called “seer,” clarifying the term in the source.

2-chronicles-33:18:13.summary: “The rest of Solomon’s acts… written” uses the same regnal source formula.

2-chronicles-33:19:0.summary: God forgives those who confess sins, a principle behind God hearing Manasseh’s prayer despite his sins.

2-chronicles-33:19:1.summary: Saul the persecutor praying loosely parallels a great sinner turning to prayer.

2-chronicles-33:19:2.summary: Grace bringing justification from many trespasses fits Manasseh’s many sins and heard prayer only in principle.

2-chronicles-33:19:3.summary: People not holding to God’s ordinances shares no specific element with Manasseh’s prayer and record.

2-chronicles-33:19:5.summary: “Before I was humbled, I did wrong” loosely fits Manasseh’s sins before his humbling.

2-chronicles-33:19:6.summary: God accepts the prayers of the upright, generally related to Manasseh’s heard prayer.

2-chronicles-33:19:7.summary: Zedekiah felt no shame before the prophet, contrasting with Manasseh’s eventual turning.

2-chronicles-33:19:8.summary: God humbled the psalmist in truth, a general theme of chastening like Manasseh’s.

2-chronicles-33:19:10.summary: “It is good for me that Thou didst humble me” fits Manasseh’s humbling in principle.

2-chronicles-33:19:11.summary: Northerners feeling shame and coming to Jerusalem shares nothing specific with Manasseh’s record.

2-chronicles-33:20:0.summary: “Manasseh begot Amos” names Manasseh and his son, who reigned after him (Amon).

2-chronicles-33:20:2.summary: Hezekiah “lay down with his fathers… his son Manasseh reigned in his place,” the same formula.

2-chronicles-33:20:3.summary: The genealogy lists “Amon his son,” Manasseh’s successor.

2-chronicles-33:21:3.summary: Manasseh’s accession uses the same age-and-length formula as Amon’s.

2-chronicles-33:21:0.summary: Life is a vapor appearing briefly, a reflection loosely suited to Amon’s two-year reign.

2-chronicles-33:21:2.summary: The rich fool’s sudden death shares no specific element with Amon’s accession details.

2-chronicles-33:22:4.summary: Kings details Manasseh’s idols and evil, which Amon followed as his father had done.

2-chronicles-33:22:0.summary: Children warned not to walk in their fathers’ ordinances, the opposite of Amon following Manasseh.

2-chronicles-33:22:2.summary: Manasseh’s evil and idols, which Amon imitated and served, are described here.
2-chronicles-33:22:2.why: Defines the father’s sins Amon copied.

2-chronicles-33:22:3.summary: Josiah destroyed the carved and cast objects his father Amon had served.

2-chronicles-33:22:5.summary: Isaiah mocks making and worshiping carved idols, generally relevant to Amon serving idols.

2-chronicles-33:23:1.summary: Manasseh’s prayer and turning back is recorded, the humbling Amon failed to imitate.

2-chronicles-33:23:2.summary: Evil people go from bad to worse, loosely like Amon multiplying transgression.

2-chronicles-33:23:4.summary: They hardened their neck beyond their fathers, loosely like Amon exceeding in transgression.

2-chronicles-33:23:5.summary: Manasseh’s accession age shares only the name with Amon’s failure to humble himself.

2-chronicles-33:23:6.summary: Ahaz departed further from the Lord when afflicted, like Amon refusing to humble himself.

2-chronicles-33:24:0.summary: God’s kindness and severity to Gentiles shares nothing specific with Amon’s assassination.

2-chronicles-33:24:1.summary: Amaziah was killed by a conspiracy after departing from the Lord, a similar royal assassination.

2-chronicles-33:24:3.summary: Ishbosheth (here Mephibosheth) was struck in his house by his men, a loose parallel to Amon’s murder.

2-chronicles-33:24:4.summary: Men of bloodshed will not live out half their days, loosely fitting Amon’s short reign.

2-chronicles-33:24:5.summary: Joash’s servants attacked him and killed him on his bed, closely parallel to Amon struck by servants in his house.

2-chronicles-33:25:0.summary: The guilty killer must be put to death, generally underlying the people striking Amon’s assassins.

2-chronicles-33:25:1.summary: Bloodshed is atoned only by the killer’s blood, generally related to executing Amon’s killers.

2-chronicles-33:25:2.summary: Whoever sheds man’s blood shall have his shed, a general principle behind punishing the assassins.

2-chronicles-33:25:3.summary: “The people of the land” made Jehoahaz king in his father’s place, the same phrase and action.
2-chronicles-33:25:3.why: People of the land install kings.

2-chronicles-33:25:4.summary: Josiah begins his reign, continuing directly from his installation by the people.

2-chronicles-33:25:5.summary: “All the people of the land” made Uzziah king in his father’s place, the same pattern.

2-chronicles-34:1:2.summary: Manasseh’s accession uses the same age-and-length formula as Josiah’s.

2-chronicles-34:1:0.summary: Jeremiah’s ministry is dated to Josiah’s thirteenth year, the same king.

2-chronicles-34:1:1.summary: Zephaniah prophesied in the days of Josiah son of Amon, the same king.

2-chronicles-34:1:3.summary: The people of the land made Josiah king, the immediate prelude to his reign.

2-chronicles-34:1:4.summary: A prophet foretold a son of David’s house, “Josiah by name,” who would defile the altar.

2-chronicles-34:1:5.summary: A wise youth is better than a foolish old king, loosely fitting the boy-king Josiah.
2-chronicles-34:1:5.why: Value of a wise young ruler.

2-chronicles-34:1:6.summary: Matthew’s genealogy names Josiah as son of Amon (“Amos”) and father of Jechoniah.

2-chronicles-34:1:7.summary: The genealogy lists “Josiah his son” and Josiah’s sons.

2-chronicles-34:1:8.summary: Uzziah made king at sixteen loosely parallels Josiah as a young king.

2-chronicles-34:1:9.summary: Solomon as “a little child” seeking wisdom loosely parallels Josiah’s youthful reign.

2-chronicles-34:1:10.summary: The child Samuel growing in favour shares no specific element with Josiah’s accession.

2-chronicles-34:1:11.summary: Joash was seven when he became king and reigned forty years in Jerusalem, a parallel child-king formula.

2-chronicles-34:1:13.summary: The child Samuel ministering shares only youth with Josiah’s accession.

2-chronicles-34:2:0.summary: Hezekiah did right before the Lord according to David his father, the same commendation.

2-chronicles-34:2:1.summary: “Do not turn aside… to the right or to the left” matches Josiah’s turning neither way.

2-chronicles-34:2:2.summary: Jehoshaphat walked in his father’s earlier ways, a similar commendation.

2-chronicles-34:2:3.summary: Asa did what was good and right before the Lord, a similar formula.

2-chronicles-34:2:4.summary: Keep the law so “that you do not turn aside to the right or to the left,” the same phrase.

2-chronicles-34:2:5.summary: David did right and did not turn aside from God’s commands, the model Josiah followed.

2-chronicles-34:2:6.summary: “Turn neither to the right nor to the left,” the identical expression.

2-chronicles-34:2:7.summary: Not turning aside “to the right hand or to the left” from God’s words matches the source.

2-chronicles-34:2:9.summary: The law of the king: not turning aside to the right or left, which Josiah exemplified.

2-chronicles-34:2:10.summary: “Do not turn to the right or the left” shares the source’s idiom of steadfastness.

2-chronicles-34:2:11.summary: Not turning aside “to the right hand or to the left” from the law repeats the idiom.

2-chronicles-34:2:13.summary: Sirach praises the remembrance of Josiah, the same king commended here.

2-chronicles-34:3:0.summary: Amon served Manasseh’s idols, the background against which Josiah sought the Lord and purged idols.

2-chronicles-34:3:1.summary: “If you seek Him, He shall be found,” a general parallel to Josiah beginning to seek the Lord.
2-chronicles-34:3:1.why: Promise to those who seek God.

2-chronicles-34:3:2.summary: The people still worshiped at the high places under Manasseh, the high places Josiah cleansed.

2-chronicles-34:3:3.summary: “Those who seek me will find me” loosely relates to Josiah seeking the Lord.

2-chronicles-34:3:4.summary: Hezekiah removed high places, pillars and groves, the same reform Josiah undertook.

2-chronicles-34:3:5.summary: Knowing the scriptures from infancy loosely parallels Josiah seeking God while a boy.

2-chronicles-34:3:6.summary: A young man sets his way right by God’s words, loosely fitting the young Josiah.

2-chronicles-34:3:7.summary: Solomon is urged to know and seek “the God of your fathers,” as Josiah sought the God of David.
2-chronicles-34:3:7.why: Same call to seek the fathers’ God.

2-chronicles-34:3:8.summary: The prophecy names Josiah as the one who would destroy the high-place priests’ altar, fulfilled in his purge.

2-chronicles-34:3:9.summary: Seeking God’s kingdom first shares only the verb “seek” with Josiah seeking the Lord.

2-chronicles-34:3:10.summary: Remembering the Creator in youth loosely parallels Josiah seeking God as a boy.

2-chronicles-34:3:11.summary: God threatens to destroy pillars and wooden images, related to the objects Josiah cleansed.

2-chronicles-34:3:13.summary: Solomon as a tender child undertaking great work loosely parallels the boy Josiah.

2-chronicles-34:3:14.summary: Altars in Jerusalem were demolished under Hezekiah, the same kind of cleansing Josiah began.

2-chronicles-34:3:15.summary: Solomon is “young and tender” for a great work, loosely like the boy Josiah.

2-chronicles-34:3:16.summary: Josiah shattered pillars and destroyed groves, the parallel account of his purge.

2-chronicles-34:4:8.summary: Josiah pulled down groves and altars and cut idols into fine pieces, the same campaign continued.

2-chronicles-34:4:0.summary: Moses burned and ground the calf fine and scattered it, like Josiah pulverizing and scattering idols.

2-chronicles-34:4:1.summary: God threatens to destroy pillars and wooden images, related to Josiah’s destruction of idols.

2-chronicles-34:4:3.summary: Josiah pulled down altars, including Manasseh’s, and threw their dust into the Kidron, the parallel purge.

2-chronicles-34:4:4.summary: Asa removed altars and idols from Judah’s cities, a similar royal purge.

2-chronicles-34:4:5.summary: Altar stones cut down like fine dust and idols cut down match Josiah pulverizing altars and idols.
2-chronicles-34:4:5.why: Prophetic image of the same purge.

2-chronicles-34:4:6.summary: Israel was commanded to overthrow the gods and shatter their pillars, as Josiah did.

2-chronicles-34:4:7.summary: Burning the graven images of the nations’ gods is the law behind Josiah’s destruction of carved objects.

2-chronicles-34:4:9.summary: Moses ground the calf fine as dust and cast it out, paralleling Josiah pulverizing idols.

2-chronicles-34:4:10.summary: Manasseh rebuilt high places, Baal pillars and groves, the very things Josiah destroyed.

2-chronicles-34:4:11.summary: Grinding enemies fine like dust shares the image of pulverizing but concerns enemies, not idols.

2-chronicles-34:4:12.summary: Jehu pulled down Baal’s pillars and house, a parallel destruction of Baal worship.

2-chronicles-34:4:13.summary: Pull down their altars, break pillars, cut down sacred groves, burn images—the exact program Josiah carried out.

2-chronicles-34:5:1.summary: Both concern the land being defiled and cleansed, but Numbers addresses bloodguilt, not idolatrous altars or burned bones.
2-chronicles-34:5:1.why: Background on the idea of purifying a defiled land.

2-chronicles-34:5:2.summary: The same purge by Josiah continues: he pulls down groves, altars and high places, then returns to Jerusalem.
2-chronicles-34:5:2.why: Completes the account of Josiah's cleansing campaign.

2-chronicles-34:5:3.summary: Jeremiah foresees “the bones of the priests” brought out of tombs, matching the burning of priests’ bones in Josiah's purge.
2-chronicles-34:5:3.why: Prophetic echo of the desecration of idolatrous priests' bones.

2-chronicles-34:5:4.summary: Judah's half-hearted return contrasts with outward cleansing, but the verse names no reform or bones.
2-chronicles-34:5:4.why: Hints that outward reform did not change hearts.

2-chronicles-34:5:5.summary: The Greek reads “a land not wetted” by rain, so the link to cleansing the land is lost.
2-chronicles-34:5:5.why: No real link in the Greek-based wording.

2-chronicles-34:5:7.summary: Kings' parallel: Josiah took bones from the tombs and burned them on the altar, defiling it.
2-chronicles-34:5:7.why: Parallel account with fulfilled prophecy details.

2-chronicles-34:5:8.summary: A call for Jerusalem to wash its heart clean loosely parallels cleansing Judah and Jerusalem.

2-chronicles-34:6:0.summary: Hezekiah also reached out to Ephraim and Manasseh, a precedent for a Judean king acting in northern territory.
2-chronicles-34:6:0.why: Earlier royal outreach to the northern tribes.

2-chronicles-34:6:1.summary: Isaiah's plowed mountains and pasture share nothing with Josiah's reform in northern cities.

2-chronicles-34:6:2.summary: Hezekiah's runners went through Ephraim and Manasseh to Zaboulon; shared northern tribal names only.
2-chronicles-34:6:2.why: Shows earlier contact with the northern tribes.

2-chronicles-34:6:4.summary: Sharpening tools at the Philistine forge has no link to Josiah's reform in northern cities.
2-chronicles-34:6:4.why: Link depends on Hebrew wording not present here.

2-chronicles-34:6:5.summary: Hezekiah's purge likewise destroyed high places and altars in Ephraim and Manasseh, a close precedent for Josiah's reach north.
2-chronicles-34:6:5.why: Parallel reform by an earlier king in the same territory.

2-chronicles-34:6:6.summary: A proverb about false witness has no connection to Josiah's purge of northern cities.

2-chronicles-34:7:0.summary: Both describe cutting down “sacred groves” and demolishing high places and altars, then returning home.
2-chronicles-34:7:0.why: Hezekiah's reform as a model for Josiah's.

2-chronicles-34:7:1.summary: Moses broke the calf in pieces until it became “fine,” as Josiah cut the idols into fine pieces.
2-chronicles-34:7:1.why: Distinctive image of grinding idols to dust.

2-chronicles-34:7:2.summary: Introduces Josiah's reign; same king but no specific link to the purge itself.

2-chronicles-34:8:0.summary: Mentions a royal official “over the records,” the office Joah holds, but different people and era.

2-chronicles-34:8:1.summary: Gedaliah son of Ahikam is named, but Shaphan does not appear in the shown text.
2-chronicles-34:8:1.why: Family link not evident from the text.

2-chronicles-34:8:2.summary: Ahikam “son of Shaphan” protects Jeremiah, connecting to Shaphan's family.
2-chronicles-34:8:2.why: Traces Shaphan's family in later history.

2-chronicles-34:8:3.summary: “Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe” names the same royal scribe Shaphan.
2-chronicles-34:8:3.why: Shows Shaphan's household in Jeremiah's time.

2-chronicles-34:8:4.summary: Judgment on Ahab and Zedekiah shares no names or events with Josiah's officials.
2-chronicles-34:8:4.why: No connection visible in the text.

2-chronicles-34:8:5.summary: Both mention a “city ruler,” but different people and contexts.
2-chronicles-34:8:5.why: Shows the office of city ruler.

2-chronicles-34:8:6.summary: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah is a different person; only a similar name is shared.

2-chronicles-34:8:7.summary: Elasah “son of Shaphan” serves as envoy, linking to Shaphan's family.
2-chronicles-34:8:7.why: Shaphan's family in later royal service.

2-chronicles-34:8:8.summary: Gedaliah “son of Ahikam son of Shaphan” receives Jeremiah, continuing Shaphan's family line.

2-chronicles-34:8:9.summary: Jehoshaphat was “recorder” under David, the same office Joah holds, but different persons.

2-chronicles-34:8:10.summary: Jaazaniah son of Shaphan among idolatrous elders is likely a different Shaphan; only the name matches.
2-chronicles-34:8:10.why: Name coincidence rather than a clear link.

2-chronicles-34:8:12.summary: Dates Jeremiah's call to Josiah's thirteenth year, the same reign as this eighteenth-year event.

2-chronicles-34:8:13.summary: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah is a different person from Maasias the city ruler.

2-chronicles-34:8:14.summary: Josaphat was “recorder” under David, the same office as Joah's, but different people.

2-chronicles-34:9:0.summary: Ephraim and Manasse appear in Hezekiah's outreach, as they contribute silver here; only tribal names shared.
2-chronicles-34:9:0.why: Northern tribes' involvement in Judean worship.

2-chronicles-34:9:1.summary: Hilkiah appears as a ruler of God's house giving for Josiah's Passover.

2-chronicles-34:9:2.summary: People of Ephraim and Manasse joined Hezekiah's Passover; shared tribal names and northern participation only.

2-chronicles-34:9:3.why: Same officials in the next stage of the story.

2-chronicles-34:9:4.summary: Shaphan reports that Hilkiah gave him a book, continuing this same temple mission.

2-chronicles-34:9:5.summary: Hezekiah's reform involved Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasse, the same groups that gave silver here.
2-chronicles-34:9:5.why: Same regions joined in an earlier reform.

2-chronicles-34:9:7.summary: Hilkiah leads the delegation to Huldah, same high priest in the same episode.
2-chronicles-34:9:7.why: Follows Hilkiah's role in the story.

2-chronicles-34:9:9.summary: As the silver brought into the Lord's house was taken out, Hilkiah found the book of the law.
2-chronicles-34:9:9.why: Directly continues this handing-over of silver.

2-chronicles-34:9:10.summary: Paul's list of virtues has no connection to collecting silver for temple repairs.

2-chronicles-34:9:11.summary: Chelkias the high priest and the doorpost guards act under Josiah, the same priest and gate guards.
2-chronicles-34:9:11.why: Kings' account of the same high priest's role.

2-chronicles-34:10:1.summary: Silver was given “to those doing the work” to strengthen the Lord's house, matching this verse closely.

2-chronicles-34:10:2.summary: Silver placed in workers' hands to pay carpenters and builders for strengthening the Lord's house.
2-chronicles-34:10:2.why: Close parallel in temple repair procedure.

2-chronicles-34:10:3.summary: Silver given to stonecutters and craftsmen for timber in rebuilding the temple; general building theme.
2-chronicles-34:10:3.why: Later temple building with similar funding.

2-chronicles-34:11:0.summary: Manasseh's desecration of the Lord's house explains damage, though the source speaks of buildings destroyed by kings.
2-chronicles-34:11:0.why: Background on why repairs were needed; truncated text.

2-chronicles-34:11:1.summary: Amon's idolatry belongs to the kings whose neglect left buildings ruined; no mention of buildings.

2-chronicles-34:12:0.summary: Workers were not called to account because they acted in trustworthiness, as these men were faithful.
2-chronicles-34:12:0.why: Same honesty of temple workers in Joash's repair.

2-chronicles-34:12:1.summary: Levites praised the Lord with instruments, echoing Levites skilled in instruments of song.

2-chronicles-34:12:2.summary: Levites including a Zacharias minister with instruments, but a different era and duty.

2-chronicles-34:12:3.summary: Levitical singers chosen to praise the Lord; general musician theme.

2-chronicles-34:12:4.summary: Anania was a truthful man given oversight, loosely like the faithful overseers here.

2-chronicles-34:12:5.summary: Stewards must be found faithful, a general principle echoing the faithful workers.

2-chronicles-34:12:6.summary: Under Hezekiah things were done “faithfully” with a Levite as “overseer,” matching faithful Levite overseers here.

2-chronicles-34:12:7.summary: David's organization of Levitical musicians with instruments; general background only (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:12:8.summary: A trustworthy man will be blessed; general faithfulness theme.

2-chronicles-34:12:10.summary: Singers from Kaath's sons ministered with instruments; Kohath link is general (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:12:11.summary: Levites from Merari's sons and a Zacharias appointed as musicians, general background (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:13:12.summary: Levites served as supervisors “over the works,” “scribes and judges,” and “gatekeepers,” matching this list.

2-chronicles-34:13:0.summary: The Greek speaks of the strength of enemies, not burden-bearers, so the link is lost.
2-chronicles-34:13:0.why: No real link in the Greek-based wording.

2-chronicles-34:13:1.summary: Solomon's “burden bearers” and taskmasters over the people parallel the overseers of burden-bearers here.

2-chronicles-34:13:2.summary: Divisions of Levitical gatekeepers; general background (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:13:3.summary: Idithon's sons with instruments at the gate; general Levitical roles.

2-chronicles-34:13:4.summary: A list of gatekeepers; shares only the role.

2-chronicles-34:13:5.summary: Levitical brethren named as gatekeepers; shared role only.

2-chronicles-34:13:6.summary: Levites and gatekeepers stationed by David's ordinance; general organization theme.

2-chronicles-34:13:7.summary: “The scribes and the Levites” serve under Jehoshaphat's judges; shared role terms only.

2-chronicles-34:13:8.summary: Chief priests gathering at Caiaphas's court has no link to Levitical overseers of temple work.

2-chronicles-34:13:9.summary: Abdedom and Ossa were gatekeepers; shared role only.

2-chronicles-34:13:10.summary: Rebuke of false scribes shares only the word “scribes.”

2-chronicles-34:13:11.summary: Esdras the scribe, with Levites and gatekeepers, shares the roles listed here.

2-chronicles-34:13:13.summary: Provisions for timber workers on Solomon's temple; general building labor theme.

2-chronicles-34:13:14.summary: Solomon's chief supervisors drove the people's work, like overseers of the works.

2-chronicles-34:14:0.summary: Statutes given “by the hand of Moses” echo the phrase describing the found law book, but no event link.

2-chronicles-34:14:2.summary: Esdras set his heart to seek the law; a later rediscovery of the law, but no direct link.

2-chronicles-34:14:4.summary: Josiah's deeds are linked to the Lord's law; same king, but no reference to the book's discovery.

2-chronicles-34:14:5.summary: Judgment for not desiring the law of the Lord; general theme of neglected law.

2-chronicles-34:14:8.summary: Delight and meditation in the Lord's law; general theme.

2-chronicles-34:14:10.why: Importance of the book of the law.

2-chronicles-34:14:11.summary: Hezekiah's provision for the Lord's house ministry; only a loose link to temple contributions.

2-chronicles-34:14:12.summary: The silver brought into God's house was handed to Hilkiah, the same silver and priest in this scene.

2-chronicles-34:14:13.summary: Completing rites according to the Lord's law in Luke shares only the phrase “the Lord’s law.”

2-chronicles-34:14:14.summary: Rehoboam abandoning commandments has no specific link to finding the book of the law.

2-chronicles-34:14:15.summary: Aaron obeying what the Lord directed Moses shares only a general mention of Moses.

2-chronicles-34:16:1.summary: Officials report to the king and a scroll is read before him, paralleling Shaphan bringing the book to Josiah.
2-chronicles-34:16:1.why: Sets Josiah beside Jehoiakim's scroll episode.

2-chronicles-34:18:0.summary: “This book of the law” is to be meditated upon; shared phrase only.

2-chronicles-34:18:1.summary: Speaking God's testimonies before kings loosely parallels reading the law before the king.

2-chronicles-34:18:2.summary: The king is to read the law all his days; loosely parallels the law read before Josiah.
2-chronicles-34:18:2.why: The king's duty to read the law.

2-chronicles-34:18:3.summary: A scroll is reported and read aloud before the king, closely paralleling Shaphan reading the book before Josiah.

2-chronicles-34:18:4.summary: Love and meditation on the law; general devotional theme.

2-chronicles-34:19:2.summary: Hezekiah also “heard” and “tore his garments,” the same royal response of grief.

2-chronicles-34:19:9.summary: Jehoiakim and his servants heard the scroll yet did not tear their garments, the opposite of Josiah.

2-chronicles-34:19:0.summary: Joshua tore his clothes in distress; shared gesture of mourning in a different situation.

2-chronicles-34:19:1.summary: The curse on those not doing all written “in the book of the law” relates to the king's alarm.

2-chronicles-34:19:3.summary: The law brings knowledge of sin; loose theme of conviction by the law.

2-chronicles-34:19:5.summary: “Through law comes knowledge of sin,” loosely matching the king's response to hearing the law.

2-chronicles-34:19:6.summary: Covenant blessings and curses likely in the book read; shown text only gives blessings (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:19:7.summary: Kings' parallel: the Lord notes Josiah heard, felt shame, and did “rend your garments.”

2-chronicles-34:19:8.summary: Dying to law to live to God has no specific link to Josiah tearing his garments.

2-chronicles-34:19:10.summary: “Tear your hearts, not your garments” comments on the gesture of tearing garments.

2-chronicles-34:20:1.summary: “Ahikam son of Shaphan” appears again protecting Jeremiah, the same official.

2-chronicles-34:20:2.summary: Gedaliah's oath names no one from Josiah's delegation in the shown text.
2-chronicles-34:20:2.why: Family link not evident in text.

2-chronicles-34:20:3.summary: Coming to Gedaliah at Mizpah names no one from this verse.

2-chronicles-34:20:4.summary: Godolias “son of Achikam son of Saphan” is the grandson of Shaphan and son of Ahikam named here.
2-chronicles-34:20:4.why: Traces the family into the exile era.

2-chronicles-34:20:5.summary: The Greek text has only “the king sent men to Egypt,” lacking the names that would link it.

2-chronicles-34:20:6.summary: A warning to Gedaliah about Ishmael names none of the officials listed here.

2-chronicles-34:21:0.summary: Elders come to inquire of the Lord through a prophet; general inquiry theme (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:21:1.summary: Judah suffered because it abandoned the God of their fathers; general sin-and-judgment theme.

2-chronicles-34:21:2.summary: “Ask the Lord about us” parallels Josiah's “seek the Lord concerning me,” a king consulting a prophet.
2-chronicles-34:21:2.why: Royal inquiry in a time of crisis.

2-chronicles-34:21:3.summary: Manasseh taken captive as judgment; background to the wrath Josiah fears.

2-chronicles-34:21:4.summary: Jehoshaphat asks to “inquire of the Lord” through a prophet; general inquiry theme.

2-chronicles-34:21:5.summary: The Song of Moses describes Israel forsaking God and provoking His anger (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:21:6.summary: Hezekiah likewise says the Lord became fiercely angry with Judah; similar admission of wrath.

2-chronicles-34:21:7.summary: God's wrath revealed against ungodliness; general wrath theme.

2-chronicles-34:21:9.summary: People went to inquire of God through a seer; general practice of consulting prophets.

2-chronicles-34:21:10.summary: God foretells wrath when the people forsake His covenant; matches the theme of burning anger (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:21:11.summary: “The law brings wrath” loosely fits wrath tied to the found book.

2-chronicles-34:21:12.summary: Israel's exile because they sinned; relates to “all who are left in Israel.”

2-chronicles-34:21:13.summary: The Lord's anger blazes with “all the curses of this covenant which are written in this book” (truncated).
2-chronicles-34:21:13.why: The book's own warning of wrath.

2-chronicles-34:21:14.summary: A plea to pray to the Lord for the few survivors loosely echoes concern for those left.

2-chronicles-34:21:15.summary: Curses come if Israel does not keep and do all His commandments, the failure Josiah confesses.

2-chronicles-34:21:16.summary: Hezekiah sends his scribe and priests to a prophet to plead “for those who remain,” a close parallel.
2-chronicles-34:21:16.why: Parallel royal delegation to a prophet.

2-chronicles-34:21:17.summary: Covenant curses for disobedience; general background to God's anger (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:21:19.summary: Elders come to question the Lord, and the fathers' lawlessness is recounted (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:21:20.summary: People come to Moses to seek judgment from God; general inquiry theme.
2-chronicles-34:21:20.why: Seeking God's word through a mediator.

2-chronicles-34:21:21.summary: Warning of perishing if the heart turns to other gods; general covenant theme.

2-chronicles-34:22:0.summary: Miriam is called “the prophetess,” another woman prophet, but no further link.

2-chronicles-34:22:1.summary: Anna is “a prophetess” and widow; shared title only.

2-chronicles-34:22:2.summary: Elizabeth's Spirit-filled blessing of Mary has no specific link to Huldah.

2-chronicles-34:22:4.summary: Philip's daughters prophesied; shared theme of women prophets.

2-chronicles-34:22:5.summary: Deborah, “a prophetess, the wife of” Lappidoth, is introduced in the same pattern as Huldah.

2-chronicles-34:23:2.summary: Jeremiah tells the envoys “Say this to Zedekiah,” a prophet answering a king's delegation (truncated).

2-chronicles-34:24:2.summary: Warning against transgressing the covenant and serving other gods; general background.
